title: Convergence and mixed-precision preconditioning for the naive Jacobi eigenvalue algorithm
summary: The paper studies a Jacobi-type method for the eigenvalue problem of general complex matrices with simple eigenvalues. The method applies elementary triangular similarity transformations in order to annihilate selected off-diagonal elements and, when convergent, produces highly accurate eigenvalues. We give a new proof of its asymptotic quadratic convergence and derive an explicit, verifiable bound that describes the region in which this convergence is guaranteed. To make the method applicable well beyond matrices already close to the diagonal form, we introduce a preconditioning strategy. We use two types of preconditioners, both based on theoretical convergence results. The preconditioner is computed at lower precision to reduce computational cost, the associated similarity transformation is applied either at working or at higher precision, to preserve spectral information, while the main algorithm performs at working precision. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the resulting algorithm is robust and produces very accurate eigenvalues.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a Jacobi-type method for eigenvalues of general complex matrices, with a new convergence proof, explicit convergence region bounds, and a preconditioning strategy using mixed precision to improve robustness and accuracy.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust, highly accurate eigenvalue solver for general complex matrices that works well even for matrices far from diagonal form, not just those already close to convergence.
AI.method: Jacobi-type method using elementary triangular similarity transformations; new asymptotic quadratic convergence proof with explicit verifiable bound; preconditioning strategy using two types of preconditioners computed at lower precision with transformations applied at working or higher precision, while the main algorithm runs at working precision.
AI.result: The preconditioned algorithm is robust and produces very accurate eigenvalues, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed mixed-precision preconditioning strategy successfully extends the applicability of the Jacobi-type method beyond the region of asymptotic quadratic convergence, yielding a robust and accurate eigenvalue solver for general complex matrices.

title: A virtual element method for Darcy's problem coupled with a heat equation
summary: In two dimensions, we develop a virtual element method to solve the Darcy's problem coupled with a nonlinear heat equation. This coupled model may allow for thermal diffusion and viscosity as a function of temperature. Under standard discretization assumptions and appropriate assumptions on the data, we prove the well posedness of the proposed numerical scheme. We also derive optimal error estimates under suitable regularity assumptions for the solution and appropriate assumptions on the data. We conclude with a series of numerical tests performed on different families of meshes that complement the theoretical findings.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a virtual element method for solving coupled Darcy's problem and nonlinear heat equation in 2D, proving well-posedness and optimal error estimates with numerical validation.
AI.motivation: To solve a coupled Darcy flow and nonlinear heat transfer problem where thermal diffusion and viscosity depend on temperature, requiring a robust numerical method.
AI.method: A virtual element method (VEM) is developed for the coupled system in two dimensions, with standard discretization assumptions and appropriate data assumptions.
AI.result: Proved well-posedness of the numerical scheme and derived optimal error estimates under suitable regularity assumptions.
AI.conclusion: Numerical tests on various mesh families confirm the theoretical results, validating the method's effectiveness.

title: Hierarchical Log-Gaussian Relaxation on a Fixed D3Q125 Velocity Set
summary:
We develop a hierarchical order-resolved relaxation model for a fixed D3Q125 discrete-velocity kinetic formulation. Conventional adaptive collision models often use one scalar rarefaction or nonequilibrium indicator for all retained moment orders, thereby coupling distinct kinetic sectors. Here, a shared macroscopic-gradient background is combined separately with second-, third-, and fourth-order thermodynamic nonequilibrium indicators to define effective measures K2, K3, and K4, each driving its own log-Gaussian relaxation spectrum.
  Pure-order perturbation tests verify selective activation, with nonmatching sectors remaining at roundoff level. Homogeneous mixed-order, amplitude, and composition tests show lower residual nonequilibrium than a common-sensor model while preserving positive populations. In a smooth periodic compression wave at the stated reference discretization and in the TNE-only sensor limit, the peak total nonequilibrium intensity is reduced by 6.565%, with reductions throughout the domain and in all retained moment sectors.
  Additional timestep, transport-discretization, relaxation-spectrum, uniform-boost, long-time, and shear-wave studies show that the sign of the hierarchical correction is robust over the tested configurations, while its magnitude depends on timestep, transport scheme, sensor frame, and relaxation spectrum. The periodic benchmarks preserve the principal global invariants to floating-point accuracy and remain positive. These results establish the mechanism and numerical behavior of order-resolved activation on a fixed velocity set; independent kinetic-reference validation is still required before claiming universal accuracy improvement.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a hierarchical order-resolved relaxation model for D3Q125 discrete-velocity kinetic formulations, using separate second-, third-, and fourth-order thermodynamic nonequilibrium indicators (K2, K3, K4) with independent log-Gaussian relaxation spectra, demonstrating selective activation and reduced nonequilibrium compared to common-sensor models.
AI.motivation: Conventional adaptive collision models use a single scalar rarefaction or nonequilibrium indicator for all retained moment orders, coupling distinct kinetic sectors and limiting accuracy.
AI.method: A hierarchical order-resolved relaxation model is developed where a shared macroscopic-gradient background is combined separately with second-, third-, and fourth-order thermodynamic nonequilibrium indicators to define K2, K3, and K4, each driving its own log-Gaussian relaxation spectrum.
AI.result: Pure-order perturbation tests verify selective activation. The model shows lower residual nonequilibrium than a common-sensor model while preserving positivity. In a smooth periodic compression wave, peak total nonequilibrium intensity is reduced by 6.565% across all moment sectors. Global invariants are preserved to floating-point accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The mechanism and numerical behavior of order-resolved activation on a fixed velocity set are established; independent kinetic-reference validation is still required before claiming universal accuracy improvement.

title: High-Order Exponential Integrators with Improved Uniform Accuracy for Charged-Particle in a Perpendicular Strong Magnetic Field
summary: This paper considers a class of charged-particle dynamics problems in which the particle is subjected to a magnetic force, with a magnetic flux density inversely proportional to a small parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$, and a nonlinear electric force. The resulting highly oscillatory behavior poses significant challenges for numerical computation. To enhance the performance of exponential integrators (EIs), this paper employs a technique that linearizes the ordinary differential equation through a dimension-raising approach. Based on this technique, a new family of EIs is developed that achieves arbitrarily high order. For short-time simulations on the interval $[0,T]$, it is rigorously proved that the proposed method--which employs auxiliary polynomials of degree $k$ and a time step $Δt$--satisfies two distinct error bounds: $O(\varepsilon Δt^{k+1})$ and $O(\varepsilon^{k+2})$. The latter bound guarantees that the algorithm stays accurate even when the step size is of order $O(1)$. Furthermore, when a large step size $\varepsilon^{-1}Δt$ is used to simulate the long-term dynamics over $[0,\varepsilon^{-1}T]$, the numerical scheme attains a uniform convergence rate of $O(Δt^{k+1})$. Several numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a new family of high-order exponential integrators for charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic fields, achieving error bounds of O(εΔt^{k+1}), O(ε^{k+2}), and uniform O(Δt^{k+1}) for long-term simulations.
AI.motivation: Charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic fields (flux density ∝ 1/ε) exhibit highly oscillatory behavior, making numerical computation challenging. Existing exponential integrators need enhancement to handle this stiffness efficiently.
AI.method: The paper linearizes the ODE via a dimension-raising approach, then constructs a new family of exponential integrators using auxiliary polynomials of degree k. This enables arbitrarily high-order schemes.
AI.result: For short-time simulations [0,T]: error bounds O(ε Δt^{k+1}) and O(ε^{k+2}), with the latter ensuring accuracy even for step size O(1). For long-term simulations [0,ε^{-1}T] with large step size ε^{-1}Δt: uniform convergence O(Δt^{k+1}). Numerical experiments confirm theory.
AI.conclusion: The proposed dimension-raising linearization technique significantly enhances exponential integrators for charged-particle dynamics, achieving arbitrarily high order with proven error bounds for both short-time and long-time simulations.

title: yancc: A GPU-accelerated, differentiable solver for neoclassical transport in tokamaks and stellarators
summary: We present yancc, a new GPU-accelerated solver for the drift kinetic equation that computes neoclassical transport fluxes, flows, and currents in tokamaks and stellarators. The drift kinetic equation is challenging to solve numerically due to strong advection-dominance, recirculating flows, internal boundary layers, severe anisotropy, and high dimensionality. The code solves both the full four-dimensional drift kinetic equation (retaining speed-dependent collisions, energy scattering, and full interspecies coupling), and the reduced monoenergetic form. The discretization combines a Maxwell polynomial collocation grid in speed with finite differences in pitch angle and the flux surface coordinates, using a modified upwind stencil designed to improve diagonal dominance for multigrid efficiency. The resulting linear system is solved with a multigrid-preconditioned Krylov method. Built in JAX, yancc is fully differentiable, enabling gradient-based optimization and adjoint sensitivity analysis. Benchmarks against MONKES and SFINCS show agreement within 1\% across a range of collisionalities, geometries, and multi-species configurations. yancc achieves roughly an order of magnitude speedup over SFINCS on a per-scan basis while using an order of magnitude less memory, with runtime remaining nearly flat across the full range of collisionality. The combination of speed, low memory footprint, and differentiability makes yancc well suited for integration into stellarator optimization workflows, uncertainty quantification, and profile prediction.

AI.tldr: yancc is a new GPU-accelerated, differentiable solver for the drift kinetic equation that achieves ~10x speedup over existing codes (SFINCS, MONKES) with 1% accuracy, combining multigrid-preconditioned Krylov methods and upwind discretization, built in JAX for stellarator optimization.
AI.motivation: Solving the drift kinetic equation for neoclassical transport in tokamaks and stellarators is computationally challenging due to advection-dominance, recirculating flows, internal boundary layers, severe anisotropy, and high dimensionality; existing solvers are too slow for optimization workflows.
AI.method: Discretization using Maxwell polynomial collocation in speed + finite differences in pitch angle and flux coordinates with modified upwind stencil; solved via multigrid-preconditioned Krylov method; implemented in JAX for GPU acceleration and differentiability.
AI.result: Agreement within 1% against MONKES and SFINCS across collisionalities, geometries, and multi-species configurations; ~10x speedup over SFINCS with an order of magnitude less memory; runtime nearly flat across collisionality range.
AI.conclusion: yancc's speed, low memory, and differentiability make it well suited for stellarator optimization, uncertainty quantification, and profile prediction workflows.

title: Several counterexamples to kinetic Schauder estimates
summary: In this paper, we construct counterexamples to the Schauder estimate for kinetic Fokker--Planck equations, disproving \cite[Conjecture~1.3]{HW}. The conjectured estimate would control second velocity derivatives using only velocity Hölder regularity of the coefficients and forcing, with no spatial regularity. We also give a zero-forcing variant, where the same {conditions are imposed on} a bounded zeroth-order coefficient. Finally, in dimensions $d\geq 2$, we give endpoint examples showing that bounded velocity-independent forcing may produce bounded distributional stationary solutions whose second velocity derivatives are not locally bounded.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs counterexamples to the Schauder estimate for kinetic Fokker-Planck equations, disproving a conjecture about controlling second velocity derivatives using only velocity Hölder regularity without spatial regularity. It also provides zero-forcing variants and endpoint examples in d≥2 dimensions.
AI.motivation: To disprove a conjecture about Schauder estimates for kinetic Fokker-Planck equations, showing that controlling second velocity derivatives using only velocity Hölder regularity (without spatial regularity) is impossible.
AI.method: Construction of explicit counterexamples to the conjectured Schauder estimate, along with zero-forcing variants and endpoint examples in dimensions d≥2.
AI.result: Disproves Conjecture 1.3 of HW; demonstrates that velocity Hölder regularity alone is insufficient; shows bounded velocity-independent forcing can produce solutions whose second velocity derivatives are not locally bounded.
AI.conclusion: The conjectured Schauder estimate requiring only velocity Hölder regularity is false; spatial regularity is necessary for such estimates.

title: A Single-Trace Surface Integral Equation Solver for Simulation of Open Bianisotropic Metasurfaces Described by Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions
summary: A single-trace surface integral equation (SIE) solver incorporating generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) is presented for the simulation of three-dimensional (3D) open bianisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is modeled as an infinitesimally thin, non-enclosing sheet across which the GSTCs enforce the electromagnetic field discontinuities through four surface susceptibility tensors. The proposed solver uses a single set of equivalent surface currents on the sheet, in place of the two sets used by prior multi-trace formulations. The scattered fields on both faces of the sheet, expressed through SIE operators acting on these currents, are substituted into the GSTCs. The resulting system of equations is then discretized using Rao--Wilton--Glisson basis functions. This solver models an open metasurface directly, without an artificial closure, and applies to both planar and curved geometries. It is validated against analytical solutions for polarization rotation and perfect reflection, and is used to model a realistic broadband absorber whose susceptibility tensors are retrieved from full-wave simulation data. A direct comparison shows that the single-trace formulation attains lower error than a multi-trace formulation while using significantly fewer unknowns.

AI.tldr: A single-trace surface integral equation solver using generalized sheet transition conditions is presented for simulating 3D open bianisotropic metasurfaces. It models metasurfaces as infinitesimally thin sheets with single surface currents, achieving lower error and fewer unknowns than multi-trace formulations.
AI.motivation: To develop a more efficient and accurate solver for open bianisotropic metasurfaces that eliminates the need for artificial enclosure and reduces computational complexity compared to prior multi-trace formulations.
AI.method: The metasurface is modeled as an infinitesimally thin sheet using GSTCs with four surface susceptibility tensors. A single set of equivalent surface currents replaces the two sets used in multi-trace approaches. Scattered fields are expressed via SIE operators, substituted into GSTCs, and discretized with Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions.
AI.result: Validated against analytical solutions for polarization rotation and perfect reflection. Applied to model a realistic broadband absorber. The single-trace formulation achieves lower error than multi-trace formulations while using significantly fewer unknowns.
AI.conclusion: The single-trace SIE-GSTC solver offers an efficient, accurate, and direct modeling approach for 3D open bianisotropic metasurfaces on both planar and curved geometries, outperforming prior multi-trace methods.

title: A stability-preserving polytopal discontinuous Galerkin method for the Fisher-Kolmogorov model with applications to neurodegenerative diseases
summary: The Fisher-Kolmogorov model is one of the most widely used models in the study of neurodegenerative diseases, owing to its simple structure as a nonlinear reaction-diffusion equation. In particular, it is commonly employed to describe proteinopathies such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Under suitable assumptions, non-negativity of the solution is guaranteed at the continuous level, which is physically relevant since the solution represents a relative concentration. However, this property is not generally preserved at the discrete level, potentially leading to unphysical and unstable numerical approximations. In this work, we analyze a modified version of the Fisher-Kolmogorov model that stabilizes the dynamics around the unstable equilibrium $c=0$. For the spatial discretization, we adopt a discontinuous Galerkin method on polygonal and polyhedral meshes, coupled with the Crank-Nicolson scheme for time integration. We derive stability and $a$-priori error estimates for the semi-discrete problem. The theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments, including convergence studies in both two and three dimensions. Finally, we validate the model through simulations of $α$-synuclein diffusion in a two-dimensional agglomerated brain section, demonstrating the high-order accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a modified Fisher-Kolmogorov model for neurodegenerative diseases, using discontinuous Galerkin methods on polygonal/polyhedral meshes with Crank-Nicolson time integration. The modification ensures non-negative solutions at the discrete level. The authors provide stability and error analysis with numerical validation, including α-synuclein diffusion simulations in brain tissue.
AI.motivation: Standard Fisher-Kolmogorov models can produce unphysical negative concentrations at the discrete level, despite non-negativity at the continuous level. This work aims to stabilize the numerical approximation to preserve physical relevance in modeling proteinopathies like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases.
AI.method: The authors modify the Fisher-Kolmogorov model to stabilize dynamics around the unstable equilibrium c=0. They use a discontinuous Galerkin method for spatial discretization on polygonal/polyhedral meshes, coupled with Crank-Nicolson scheme for time integration. Stability and a-priori error estimates are derived for the semi-discrete problem.
AI.result: Theoretical stability and error estimates are confirmed by numerical experiments in 2D and 3D convergence studies. Validation through α-synuclein diffusion simulations in a 2D agglomerated brain section demonstrates high-order accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.
AI.conclusion: The modified Fisher-Kolmogorov model with the proposed numerical scheme effectively preserves non-negativity and stability at the discrete level, making it suitable for simulating neurodegenerative proteinopathies with high accuracy.

title: Langmuir probe and infrared thermography measurements of wide and narrow heat flux profiles in the ST40 tokamak
summary: Very narrow heat flux profiles have been observed on ST40 with decay lengths in the near scrape-off-layer (SOL) of $λ_{q,near}<$~1~mm in H-mode plasmas. Measurements from divertor Langmuir probes are compared with an infrared (IR) thermography system for upper-single null diverted plasmas in L-mode and ELM-free H-mode. SOL current to the grounded divertor targets is measured from the Langmuir probes with profiles exhibiting a similar exponential decay to $λ_{q,near}$ suggesting the near SOL heat flux is related to enhanced electron current to the divertor. Inclusion of electron current contributions to the heat flux transmission coefficient is crucial in capturing similar narrow profiles to those from the IR thermography system. Ongoing upgrades to ST40 will enable more investigations on SOL power decay lengths on inboard and outboard targets in double and single null configurations.

AI.tldr: ST40 observes very narrow heat flux profiles (λq,near < ~1 mm) in H-mode near SOL, measured by Langmuir probes and IR thermography. Electron current contributions to heat flux transmission are key to matching the narrow profiles.
AI.motivation: To understand very narrow near-SOL heat flux decay lengths observed on ST40, and to compare Langmuir probe measurements with IR thermography in L-mode and ELM-free H-mode.
AI.method: Divertor Langmuir probes (including SOL current measurement) and infrared (IR) thermography system were used to measure heat flux profiles in upper-single null diverted plasmas on ST40.
AI.result: Near-SOL heat flux decay lengths λq,near < ~1 mm in H-mode; SOL current profiles show similar exponential decay; inclusion of electron current contributions to the heat flux transmission coefficient is crucial to match IR profiles.
AI.conclusion: Electron current to the divertor enhances the near-SOL heat flux. Ongoing ST40 upgrades will allow further studies on power decay lengths in double/single null configurations.

title: On the Spatially Homogeneous Boltzmann Equation with Mass Exchange
summary: We study the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation with continuous mass exchange on $X=(0,\infty)_m\times\mathbb R^d_v$, with a Grad cut-off hard-potential collision kernel. For bounded continuous symmetric mass-exchange rates, every nonnegative initial datum with finite number, mass, and kinetic energy admits a global nonnegative $L^1$-integral weak solution in $W^{1,\infty}(0,\infty;L^1(X))$ with number and mass conserved, kinetic energy dissipated. If $\int_X (m|v|^2)^{1+δ} f_0(x)dx<\infty,$ for some $δ>0$, this higher-energy moment propagates on every finite time interval and kinetic energy is conserved through the constructed solution. Moreover, every energy-dissipating solution propagates any such moment. Under the additional $1+γ$ moment assumption, the solution is unique among all energy-dissipating $L^1$-integral weak solutions with the same initial datum. We also establish a local theory for a linearly growing mass-exchange rate. With $H_p(f)=\int_X (1+m+m|v|^2)^pfdx,$ every datum with $H_p(f_0)<\infty$, where $p\ge1+γ$ admits a conservative local $H_p$-solution. Moreover, an $H_p$-solution continues across every finite time $T$ for which $H_{1+γ}(f)\in L^1(0,T).$ This proof requires no detailed-balance or relative-entropy structures. It is based on a new two-stage bootstrap method. The first stage rules out mass concentration at $m=0$, while the second stage combines this control with collision geometry to establish uniform integrability. These estimates provide the compactness needed for the global solution and for the identification of the nonlinear collision form.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the Boltzmann equation with mass exchange, proving global existence, uniqueness, and moment propagation for weak solutions under various assumptions, using a two-stage bootstrap method that rules out mass concentration at m=0 and establishes uniform integrability.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous mathematical theory for the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation with continuous mass exchange, addressing existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions without relying on detailed-balance or relative-entropy structures.
AI.method: A two-stage bootstrap method: Stage 1 rules out mass concentration at m=0; Stage 2 combines this control with collision geometry to establish uniform integrability, providing compactness for global solutions and identification of the nonlinear collision form.
AI.result: Global nonnegative L1-integral weak solutions exist for bounded symmetric mass-exchange rates with conserved number/mass and dissipated kinetic energy; higher moments propagate; uniqueness holds under additional moment assumptions; local theory developed for linearly growing rates.
AI.conclusion: The two-stage bootstrap method successfully establishes well-posedness results for the Boltzmann equation with mass exchange without requiring detailed-balance or relative-entropy structures.

title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
summary: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in the phase-field modeling of fracture favors the use of high-order finite elements, for which matrix-free methods can provide superior performance and scalability. Here, we implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework for visco-elastoplastic materials in an open source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. We introduce a rheological fracture element assembled in series so that inelastic and fracture properties can appear to affect each other only at homogenization length scales. Numerical simulations of tensile and compressive tests are conducted for synthetic particle-matrix microstructures on an El Capitan high performance computing prototype. Results are shown to reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.

AI.tldr: This paper implements a visco-elastoplastic fracture framework using high-order finite elements with matrix-free GPU solvers, introducing a rheological fracture element that couples inelastic and fracture behavior at homogenization scales, validated on tensile/compressive tests using particle-matrix microstructures.
AI.motivation: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in phase-field fracture modeling requires high-order finite elements, and there is a need for efficient, scalable solvers (matrix-free, GPU-based) for such problems.
AI.method: Implements the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework in an open-source library with matrix-free operators, high-order finite elements, and p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. A rheological fracture element is introduced in series, coupling inelastic and fracture properties only at homogenization scales.
AI.result: Numerical simulations of tensile and compressive tests on synthetic particle-matrix microstructures (run on an El Capitan HPC prototype) reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.
AI.conclusion: The proposed GPU-accelerated high-order finite element approach effectively models visco-elastoplastic fracture with diffuse cracks, demonstrating good performance and scalability on modern HPC architectures.

title: A Damped SWIFT Method for European Option Pricing: Coefficients Decay, Truncation, and Error Analysis
summary: We introduce a damped variant of the Shannon Wavelet Inverse Fourier Technique (SWIFT) for pricing European options when the characteristic function of the underlying model is available. The key idea is to apply an exponential damping transformation to the payoff, which enables the direct computation of Fourier coefficients in the frequency domain without introducing an additional physical-domain truncation parameter. We provide a rigorous analysis of the decay of these coefficients by exploiting the singularity structure of the associated Fourier transforms. For light-tailed models, we obtain Gaussian-type decay estimates, while for semi-heavy and heavy-tailed models whose singularities are poles, algebraic branch points, or logarithmic branch points, we derive exponential decay bounds with explicit polynomial prefactors. The resulting sharp bounds make it possible to truncate the Fourier series without relying on the cumulants of the underlying density, which are often unavailable or difficult to compute in practice. We further derive an error decomposition separating projection, truncation, and quadrature errors, and translate the analysis into practical rules for selecting the damping parameter, resolution level, and truncation range. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves the accuracy of the original SWIFT method while requiring a significantly smaller number of Fourier coefficients and remaining stable in cases where the undamped method deteriorates.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a damped variant of SWIFT for pricing European options, applying exponential damping to payoff functions to compute Fourier coefficients directly. It provides rigorous decay estimates for various tail behaviors, derives error decompositions, and offers practical parameter selection rules, showing improved accuracy and stability over the original method.
AI.motivation: The original SWIFT method requires an additional physical-domain truncation parameter and relies on cumulants of the underlying density for series truncation, which are often unavailable or difficult to compute. The authors aim to eliminate these limitations and improve stability and efficiency.
AI.method: The method applies exponential damping to the payoff function, enabling direct Fourier coefficient computation in the frequency domain without a physical-domain truncation parameter. The authors analyze coefficient decay rates using singularity structures, deriving Gaussian-type decay for light-tailed models and exponential decay bounds for semi-heavy and heavy-tailed models. They also establish an error decomposition separating projection, truncation, and quadrature errors.
AI.result: The damped SWIFT method consistently improves accuracy over the original SWIFT, requires significantly fewer Fourier coefficients, and remains stable in cases where the undamped method deteriorates. Sharp decay bounds enable truncation without relying on cumulants.
AI.conclusion: The damped SWIFT variant is a more robust and efficient Fourier-based option pricing technique, with theoretical guarantees on coefficient decay and error bounds, and practical guidelines for parameter selection.

title: Gravitational Effects on Light Propagation in Linear Magnetoelectrics and Plasmas
summary: A covariant formalism for electromagnetism is used to investigate the effects of light propagation within certain material systems under the influence of a background gravitational field. Specifically, dielectric media described by linear constitutive relations, as well as magnetized plasma media, such as the magnetosphere of neutron stars, are examined. Estimates for detecting gravitational effects through precise refractive index measurements within these scenarios are provided.

AI.tldr: This paper uses covariant formalism to study how gravity affects light propagation in dielectric and magnetized plasma media, offering estimates for detecting gravitational effects via refractive index measurements.
AI.motivation: To understand how background gravitational fields influence light propagation in material systems (dielectrics and magnetized plasmas like neutron star magnetospheres) and to assess the feasibility of detecting such effects through refractive index measurements.
AI.method: A covariant formalism for electromagnetism is employed to model light propagation in linear dielectric media and magnetized plasma under a gravitational field.
AI.result: Estimates are derived for the detectability of gravitational effects via precise refractive index measurements in the examined material systems.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational influences on light propagation in these media may be measurable through high-precision refractive index experiments.

title: Quasilinear equations with exponential growth for Hörmander $q$-sub-Laplacians on stratified Lie groups
summary: We prove the existence of positive weak solutions for a quasilinear equation with exponential nonlinearity on arbitrary stratified Lie groups for \emph{horizontal $q$-Laplacians,} also called $q$-sub-Laplacians on these groups. The nonlinearity combines a concave term with an exponential growth that can be subcritical, critical, or supercritical with respect to the Trudinger--Moser inequality for Lorentz spaces on stratified Lie groups. We prove a version of this inequality in this paper. Since the problem is not variational in the natural energy space, classical minimisation or critical-point techniques do not apply directly. Positive solutions to the resulting semilinear equation are then obtained via a carefully designed Galerkin method applied to this setting. Our main theorem recovers previous known results on $\mathbb{R}^n$ in the complete range $q\in (1,\infty),$ and the previous known result on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ for $q=2n+2,$ and is extended here in the full range $q\in (1,\infty)$. Other particular and fundamental cases, including the Engel group, are discussed.

AI.tldr: The paper proves existence of positive weak solutions for a quasilinear equation with exponential nonlinearity on stratified Lie groups, using a Galerkin method and a new Trudinger-Moser inequality for Lorentz spaces.
AI.motivation: To extend existence results for quasilinear equations with exponential nonlinearity from Euclidean spaces and specific Heisenberg groups to general stratified Lie groups for the full range of $q\in(1,\infty)$.
AI.method: A Galerkin method carefully designed for stratified Lie groups, combined with a newly proven Trudinger-Moser inequality for Lorentz spaces on these groups.
AI.result: Existence of positive weak solutions is established for arbitrary stratified Lie groups over the full range $q\in(1,\infty)$, recovering and generalizing prior results on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathbb{H}^n$. Special cases including the Engel group are discussed.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for solving such quasilinear equations on stratified Lie groups, advancing beyond the limitations of classical variational methods.

title: Cycle-Consistent and Uncertainty-Aware Neural Surrogates for Tokamak Edge Plasmas
summary: The boundary and divertor plasma govern how a tokamak exhausts power and particles, setting heat fluxes, target conditions, and the onset of detachment. Predicting these quantities is essential for operating current and future devices, but edge simulations that resolve them are too slow for parameter scans, optimization, or real-time control. Machine-learning surrogates offer a fast alternative, yet most are forward-only: they cannot recover input parameters from observations or assess the reliability of their predictions. We introduce a cycle-consistent neural surrogate for edge plasmas, combining a conditional U-Net forward model with an optimization-based inverse method built on the frozen forward network. The forward model maps five control parameters to two-dimensional plasma-state fields on the SOLPS-ITER mesh; the inverse method enforces consistency between forward and inverse predictions, a self-supervised quality check needing no ground-truth labels at inference. An ensemble of multilayer perceptrons also predicts electron temperature and density profiles at the outboard midplane and divertor targets, with uncertainty estimates that flag where more simulations are needed. The forward model achieves normalized root-mean-square errors below 2.6% and Pearson correlations above 0.95 for all fields. Cycle-consistency regularization raises the average cyclical $R^2$ from 0.59 to 0.99 without degrading forward accuracy and enables recovery of the core fueling rate; all five control parameters are recovered with Pearson $r\ge0.97$. A $k$-d tree warm start yields a database completion rate above 95%, versus roughly 30% outright failures when cold-started. With about $4\times10^6$ parameters, the model produces full 2D predictions in milliseconds, five to six orders of magnitude faster than SOLPS-ITER, enabling real-time control, parameter scans, uncertainty analysis, and digital twins.

AI.tldr: A cycle-consistent neural surrogate for tokamak edge plasmas that combines a conditional U-Net forward model (mapping 5 control parameters to 2D plasma fields) with an optimization-based inverse method, achieving millisecond predictions with 2.6% error and 0.99 cyclical R².
AI.motivation: Edge plasma simulations (SOLPS-ITER) are too slow for parameter scans, optimization, or real-time control of tokamak exhaust. Existing ML surrogates are forward-only and cannot recover input parameters or assess prediction reliability.
AI.method: A conditional U-Net forward model maps 5 control parameters to 2D plasma fields on the SOLPS-ITER mesh. An optimization-based inverse method with cycle-consistency regularization enforces consistency between forward and inverse predictions. An ensemble of MLPs predicts profiles with uncertainty estimates, and a k-d tree warm start improves inverse retrieval.
AI.result: Forward model: NRMSE < 2.6%, Pearson r > 0.95. Cycle-consistency raises cyclical R² from 0.59 to 0.99. All 5 control parameters recovered with r ≥ 0.97. Database completion rate > 95% with k-d tree warm start vs ~30% failures cold-started. Predictions in milliseconds (5-6 orders faster than SOLPS-ITER).
AI.conclusion: The cycle-consistent neural surrogate enables real-time control, parameter scans, uncertainty analysis, and digital twins for tokamak edge plasmas, with both accurate forward prediction and reliable inverse parameter recovery.

title: A Mixed Discrete Cosserat Rod Formulation
summary: In this communication we propose a discrete Cosserat rod formulation in which a slender elastic rod is represented as a chain of rigid bodies (nodes) coupled by compliant elastic forces and moments acting between adjacent node pairs. Discrete dilatation, shear, torsion and curvature strain measures are evaluated from the relative kinematics of each node pair, while the constitutive behavior is expressed in compliance form through independent stress degrees of freedom. We show that the resulting model arises rigorously from a mixed Petrov--Galerkin Cosserat rod finite element formulation (FEM) at linear kinematic interpolation order when the internal virtual work is integrated by the midpoint rule and the external and inertial contributions by the trapezoidal rule. The proposed formulation inherits the robustness and the absence of locking from the underlying mixed FEM while simultaneously exposing a two-node coupling structure that mirrors discrete rod models from the computer graphics community. This is in sharp contrast to the dense coupling of strain-parameterized reduced-order models often used in soft robotic applications. Three numerical examples involving piecewise-varying cross sections, tendon-driven actuation under different spatial discretizations, and coupled longitudinal-torsional dynamics confirm the accuracy, robustness, and convergence behavior of the presented approach.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a discrete Cosserat rod formulation that models elastic rods as rigid-body chains with compliant forces, rigorously derived from a mixed Petrov-Galerkin FEM, achieving robustness without locking and exhibiting a sparse two-node coupling structure advantageous for soft robotics.
AI.motivation: To develop a discrete Cosserat rod model that combines the robustness of mixed FEM formulations (no locking) with the sparse, two-node coupling structure found in computer graphics discrete rod models, overcoming the dense coupling limitations of strain-parameterized reduced-order models commonly used in soft robotics.
AI.method: A discrete Cosserat rod is formulated as rigid-body nodes with compliant forces/moments between adjacent pairs. Strain measures (dilatation, shear, torsion, curvature) derive from relative node kinematics. The model rigorously stems from a mixed Petrov-Galerkin FEM with linear kinematic interpolation, integrating internal virtual work via midpoint rule and external/inertial terms via trapezoidal rule.
AI.result: Three numerical examples (piecewise-varying cross sections, tendon-driven actuation under varying spatial discretizations, coupled longitudinal-torsional dynamics) confirm the method's accuracy, robustness, and convergence behavior.
AI.conclusion: The proposed formulation inherits the locking-free robustness of mixed FEM while exposing a sparse two-node coupling structure, contrasting favorably with densely coupled strain-parameterized models in soft robotics.

title: Statistical Analysis of Speckle Fields
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to Physical Review E
summary: Speckles, or laser hot spots, are the intensity maxima of optically smoothed laser beams that seed instabilities, making a quantitative statistical description of speckles of interest. Earlier statistical theories estimated the number of speckles above an intensity level set for optically smoothed beams produced by random phase plates, using an ansatz that relates intensity maxima to the maxima of the real and imaginary components of the underlying complex Gaussian electric field. Here, we count speckles directly from the laser intensity field, treating it as a $χ_2^2$ random field and imposing the local maximum conditions without a single-component ansatz. We evaluate the theory for square, circular, annular, and Gaussian aperture spectra, and include induced spatial incoherence as a temporal smoothing mechanism. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the theory and show improved accuracy relative to the earlier ansatz-based formulation. Applications include a simple SBS reflectivity model using the resulting speckle statistics, and a comparison between speckle-driven and thermal noise density-fluctuation spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a refined statistical theory for counting laser speckles (intensity hot spots) directly from the intensity field as a χ²² random field, eliminating the need for a single-component ansatz. The theory is validated for various aperture spectra and temporal smoothing, showing improved accuracy over prior methods via Monte Carlo simulations, with applications to SBS reflectivity modeling and density-fluctuation spectra comparison.
AI.motivation: Speckles (laser hot spots) seed instabilities in optically smoothed laser beams, so a quantitative statistical description of speckles above a given intensity threshold is needed. Earlier theories relied on an ansatz relating intensity maxima to maxima of field components; the authors aim to develop a more direct and accurate counting method without this approximation.
AI.method: The authors treat the laser intensity field as a χ²² random field and impose local maximum conditions directly on the intensity, bypassing the earlier single-component ansatz. The theory is evaluated for square, circular, annular, and Gaussian aperture spectra, and includes induced spatial incoherence for temporal smoothing. Validation is performed via Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.result: Monte Carlo simulations confirm the new theory, showing improved accuracy compared to the earlier ansatz-based formulation. The theory works across multiple aperture spectra and with temporal smoothing effects included.
AI.conclusion: The refined speckle-counting theory provides a more accurate statistical description of laser hot spots. Applications include a simple SBS reflectivity model using the derived speckle statistics and a comparison between speckle-driven and thermal noise density-fluctuation spectra.

title: Pointwise mean-value formulas with quantitative remainder for higher-order Poisson equations
summary: Higher-order Poisson equations involve an integer power of the Laplacian and a nonzero forcing term, and appear in areas of physics and engineering such as hydrodynamics, structural engineering, and image processing. We introduce a family of mean-value formulas for solutions to higher-order Poisson equations, given in terms of linear combinations of iterated means, with an exact remainder quantified by the oscillation of the forcing term. We also prove a regularity result and a strong converse to the mean-value property, in the sense that merely locally integrable functions satisfying our formulas are regular solutions of the higher-order Poisson equation. In contrast with the homogeneous case, where the mean-value property forces smoothness, the regularity attainable here is dictated by the regularity of the forcing term. Together, our results provide a mean-value characterization of solutions to higher-order Poisson equations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces mean-value formulas for higher-order Poisson equations, with exact remainder terms involving the forcing term's oscillation, and proves regularity results and a converse to the mean-value property.
AI.motivation: To provide a mean-value characterization for solutions of higher-order Poisson equations (with nonzero forcing terms), extending known results from homogeneous higher-order equations and second-order Poisson equations.
AI.method: Derives a family of mean-value formulas using linear combinations of iterated means with an exact remainder quantified by the oscillation of the forcing term.
AI.result: (1) Mean-value formulas with exact remainder for higher-order Poisson equations. (2) A regularity result where locally integrable functions satisfying these formulas are regular solutions. (3) A strong converse showing the attainable regularity is dictated by the forcing term's regularity, not automatic smoothness.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a complete mean-value characterization of solutions to higher-order Poisson equations, bridging the gap between homogeneous and inhomogeneous cases.

title: STORM: RDMA-based Monte Carlo Transport Scheme for Distributed-Memory Particle Simulations
comment: Has been submitted to ApJS. Comments are welcome: maormiz@cs.huji.ac.il
summary: Monte Carlo particle transport enables high-fidelity astrophysical radiation and neutrino simulations - from core-collapse supernovae and neutron-star mergers to accretion flows - by handling multidimensional geometries, frequency dependence, and moving media without angular discretization. However, inter-rank communication limits scalability on unstructured meshes: standard two-sided MPI requires receivers to post receives and poll completions, creating per-iteration progress overhead that grows with the number of communication partners. Such problems have not demonstrated high scaling efficiency at $O(10^4)$ cores. We present STORM (Scalable Transport via One-sided Remote Memory), an open-source library for Monte Carlo transport on general meshes, physics, and boundary conditions. STORM provides a lock-free, mesh-independent communication layer that replaces MPI's matched-send/receive semantics with Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) - one-sided operations that write directly into a remote rank's memory without involving its CPU. Each rank pair shares a single-producer, single-consumer ring buffer; RDMA writes transfer particles while receivers remain passive. A two-sided MPI backend provides a portable fallback. In an adversarial uniform-emission benchmark, the RDMA backend sustains $>97\%$ weak-scaling and $>88\%$ strong-scaling efficiency up to 13,440~cores (112~cores per network adapter), with $1.14$-$1.27\times$ speedups over the two-sided alternative. In a Hohlraum IMC benchmark at 4480 ranks, it is $1.41\times$ faster because MPI progress overhead is reduced by $6.1\times$. By decoupling communication from physics models and mesh representations, STORM removes a barrier to scaling Monte Carlo transport in astrophysical multiphysics codes, enabling coupled radiation-hydrodynamics with energy- and angle-resolved photon or neutrino transport on dynamically evolving meshes at scale.

AI.tldr: STORM is an open-source library that replaces MPI's two-sided communication with RDMA-based one-sided operations for Monte Carlo particle transport, achieving >97% weak-scaling and >88% strong-scaling efficiency up to 13,440 cores with speedups of 1.14-1.41x over traditional MPI approaches.
AI.motivation: Standard two-sided MPI communication in Monte Carlo particle transport creates per-iteration progress overhead that scales with the number of communication partners, preventing high scaling efficiency at O(10^4) cores on unstructured meshes.
AI.method: STORM replaces MPI's matched-send/receive semantics with Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) — one-sided operations that write directly into a remote rank's memory without involving its CPU. Each rank pair uses a lock-free, single-producer single-consumer ring buffer, with RDMA writes transferring particles while receivers remain passive. A two-sided MPI backend is provided as a portable fallback.
AI.result: In an adversarial uniform-emission benchmark: >97% weak-scaling and >88% strong-scaling efficiency up to 13,440 cores (112 cores per network adapter), with 1.14-1.27x speedups. In a Hohlraum IMC benchmark at 4480 ranks: 1.41x faster with 6.1x reduction in MPI progress overhead.
AI.conclusion: By decoupling communication from physics models and mesh representations, STORM removes a barrier to scaling Monte Carlo transport in astrophysical multiphysics codes, enabling coupled radiation-hydrodynamics with energy- and angle-resolved transport on dynamically evolving meshes at scale.

title: A Hyper-Reduced Neural Network-Augmented Semi-smooth Newton Method for Nonlinear Parametric Variational Inequalities
summary:
We propose a model order reduction framework for nonlinear parametrized variational inequalities arising in computational mechanics. The high-dimensional model is written in mixed primal-dual form with projection-based complementarity conditions, leading to nonlinear nonsmooth algebraic systems solved by a semi-smooth Newton method in primal-dual form. On this basis, reduced models are constructed by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of both primal and dual solution snapshots, and the resulting reduced systems are solved by semi-smooth Newton iterations in the reduced space.
  To address cases where low-dimensional linear spaces provide limited approximation efficiency, we introduce a neural-network-augmented reduced model. Two feedforward networks learn corrections in the truncated POD coordinates of the primal and dual variables, defining a nonlinear manifold approximation that is embedded directly in the semi-smooth Newton iterations. The online cost associated with high-dimensional residual evaluations is reduced through hyper-reduction, using a sparse cubature approach based on greedy nonnegative least squares. Particular attention is paid to the interaction between hyper-reduction and the learned nonlinear manifold.
  The proposed methodology is assessed on two nonlinear variational inequalities with distinct sources of nonlinearity: a two-dimensional obstacle problem with a cubic nonlinearity in the state equation, and a three-dimensional frictional contact problem in which the Coulomb law induces a nonlinear projection in the constraint equation. Numerical results compare the high-dimensional model, the linear reduced model, the neural-network-augmented reduced model, and their hyper-reduced variants, demonstrating accurate approximations with substantial reductions in online computational cost.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a model order reduction framework for nonlinear parametrized variational inequalities, combining POD-based linear reduction with neural-network-augmented nonlinear manifold learning and hyper-reduction via sparse cubature, demonstrating accuracy and efficiency gains on 2D obstacle and 3D frictional contact problems.
AI.motivation: To address the high computational cost of solving nonlinear parametrized variational inequalities (e.g., contact, obstacle problems) in computational mechanics, and to overcome the limited approximation efficiency of low-dimensional linear subspaces in such problems.
AI.method: The framework uses POD on primal and dual snapshots for linear reduction, augments it with feedforward neural networks learning corrections on truncated POD coordinates (forming a nonlinear manifold), solves reduced systems via semi-smooth Newton iterations, and applies hyper-reduction via greedy nonnegative least squares sparse cubature to reduce online cost.
AI.result: Numerical results on a 2D obstacle problem with cubic nonlinearity and a 3D frictional contact problem with Coulomb law show that the neural-network-augmented reduced model and its hyper-reduced variant achieve accurate approximations with substantially reduced online computational cost compared to the high-dimensional model.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively reduces online computation for nonlinear variational inequalities while maintaining accuracy, especially when augmented with neural network corrections and hyper-reduction.

title: Plasma screening and configuration interaction effects induced large enhancement on L-shell photoionization cross sections and opacity
comment: Main text: 6 pages, 5 figures; Supplemental Material: 3 pages, 2 figures
summary: An opacity model that incorporates improved treatments of both plasma screening and configuration interaction (CI) effects is proposed, and a 25-30% enhancement on the iron L-shell opacity is predicted at solar interior temperatures. It is originated from the plasma screening induced 14-17% enhancement on the photoionization cross sections and the CI induced 10-20% enhancement on photoexcitation and photoionization cross sections for open L-shell ions. These explain the long-standing discrepancy between theoretical and experimental iron opacity [Nature 517, 56], and the relatively weaker enhancements on chromium and nickel opacity [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 235001] due to the sensitivity of these effects to the different L-shell electron population and plasma temperature/density. This letter provides the systematic interpretation of L-shell opacity measurements at solar interior temperatures, and advances the accurate simulation of opacity and radiative transport in high-energy-density plasma.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an opacity model combining plasma screening and configuration interaction effects, predicting a 25-30% enhancement in iron L-shell opacity at solar interior temperatures, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theoretical and experimental iron opacity measurements.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing discrepancy between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements of iron opacity at solar interior temperatures, as reported in Nature 517, 56, and to explain relatively weaker enhancements observed in chromium and nickel opacity.
AI.method: The authors developed an opacity model incorporating improved treatments of both plasma screening and configuration interaction (CI) effects, analyzing their impacts on photoionization and photoexcitation cross sections for open L-shell ions.
AI.result: A 25-30% enhancement in iron L-shell opacity was predicted, originating from: (1) plasma screening induced 14-17% enhancement on photoionization cross sections, and (2) CI induced 10-20% enhancement on photoexcitation and photoionization cross sections for open L-shell ions. Weaker enhancements were found for chromium and nickel due to sensitivity to L-shell electron population and plasma temperature/density.
AI.conclusion: This work provides systematic interpretation of L-shell opacity measurements at solar interior temperatures and advances accurate simulation of opacity and radiative transport in high-energy-density plasma.

title: Conditional scattering criteria for cylindrical threshold dynamics of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical Schrödinger equation
summary: Below-threshold scattering is studied for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical Schrödinger equation in the cylindrically symmetric class. For soliton-like compact critical elements, two linked rigidity entrances are isolated: a best fixed-axis window condition for the axial center and a low-frequency tail smallness condition. A shifted localized virial estimate and a finite-mass virial argument after axial zero-momentum normalization exclude these entrances, yielding a conditional cylindrical threshold scattering criterion via compactness reduction.

AI.tldr: This paper studies below-threshold scattering for the 3D focusing energy-critical Schrödinger equation with cylindrical symmetry. It identifies two rigidity conditions for critical elements and uses virial estimates to establish a conditional scattering criterion.
AI.motivation: To understand scattering behavior below the energy threshold for the focusing energy-critical Schrödinger equation in the cylindrically symmetric setting, particularly to characterize soliton-like compact critical elements.
AI.method: The authors isolate two rigidity entrances (axial window condition and low-frequency tail smallness), then apply a shifted localized virial estimate and a finite-mass virial argument after axial zero-momentum normalization to exclude these entrances, using compactness reduction to derive the threshold scattering criterion.
AI.result: A conditional cylindrical threshold scattering criterion is established by excluding the two identified rigidity entrances through virial-based arguments.
AI.conclusion: The given rigidity conditions can be ruled out for soliton-like compact critical elements, leading to a scattering criterion under cylindrical symmetry for the sub-threshold regime.

title: Adaptive Non-Linear Partition of Unity Methods for Scattered Data Interpolation with Discontinuities
summary: Scattered data approximation with discontinuities is challenging due to the Gibbs phenomenon, which significantly reduces accuracy near interfaces. The recently introduced Non-Linear Partition of Unity Method (NL-PUM) addresses this by combining Radial Basis Function (RBF) interpolation with a non-linear Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory (WENO) strategy. While effective, NL-PUM's performance relies heavily on two fixed hyperparameters: the RBF shape parameter and the patch radius. This work extends NL-PUM by adapting both hyperparameters locally using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) minimized via Global Optimization with Optimistic Improvement (GOOI). Our main innovation is a smoothness indicator linking a discontinuity-aware shrinkage process to LOOCV-based radius selection: patches in smooth regions remain unchanged, while those near discontinuities automatically shrink to avoid crossing the interface. The resulting method, LOOCV-NL-PUM-GOOI, requires no prior knowledge of interface geometry and introduces no extra cost beyond standard adaptive shape parameter selection. Numerical experiments on synthetic test functions with jump discontinuities and a real-data application to Norwegian Fjords elevation data confirm that this approach substantially reduces approximation error near discontinuities while preserving full accuracy in smooth regions.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes LOOCV-NL-PUM-GOOI, a method that adaptively tunes two hyperparameters (RBF shape parameter and patch radius) in the Non-Linear Partition of Unity Method using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation and Global Optimization with Optimistic Improvement, effectively handling scattered data approximation with discontinuities without prior knowledge of interface geometry.
AI.motivation: Scattered data approximation with discontinuities suffers from Gibbs phenomenon. Existing NL-PUM method works but requires manual tuning of two critical hyperparameters (RBF shape parameter and patch radius), limiting its practical applicability.
AI.method: Extends NL-PUM by locally adapting the RBF shape parameter and patch radius via LOOCV minimized through GOOI. A smoothness indicator links a discontinuity-aware shrinkage process to LOOCV-based radius selection, causing patches near discontinuities to automatically shrink while smooth regions remain unchanged.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic functions with jump discontinuities and real Norwegian Fjords elevation data show substantial error reduction near discontinuities while preserving full accuracy in smooth regions, with no extra cost beyond standard adaptive shape parameter selection.
AI.conclusion: The LOOCV-NL-PUM-GOOI method effectively removes the manual hyperparameter tuning burden, requires no prior knowledge of interface geometry, and improves approximation quality near discontinuities without sacrificing performance in smooth regions.

title: Collisionless stationary states of a stratified plasma in an expanding magnetic tube with stochastic heating
summary:
We investigate the collisionless kinetic structure of the upper solar atmosphere in the presence of an expanding magnetic field. We consider a stationary two-component plasma confined within an expanding magnetic flux tube and subject to gravity, self-electrostatic interactions, the Pannekoek-Rosseland electric field, and magnetic moment conservation. Starting from the Vlasov equation, we derive fully analytical expressions for the particle distribution functions, density profiles, and the parallel, perpendicular, and total temperature profiles.
  We show that the combined conservation of energy and magnetic moment generates a loss-cone distribution, reducing the density with respect to the corresponding unmagnetized atmosphere and producing a pronounced temperature anisotropy. For a single-temperature boundary condition, the competition between magnetic moment conservation and gravity causes the parallel temperature to develop a maximum. We derive analytical scaling laws for its location and amplitude and validate them against numerical calculations. We further show that the anisotropy persists independently of the temperature distribution at the lower boundary. In the regime of rare but intense heating events, gravitational filtering enhances the contribution of the hottest particle populations at coronal heights, while magnetic moment conservation further amplifies the resulting velocity-space anisotropy.
  This work provides a fully analytical kinetic description of the combined effects of gravitational filtering and magnetic moment conservation in an expanding coronal magnetic flux tube undergoing stochastic heating at its base. These results establish a theoretical framework for investigating the role of magnetic-field expansion in shaping the density and temperature structure of weakly collisional stellar coronae.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a fully analytical kinetic model of the solar corona in an expanding magnetic flux tube, showing that conservation of magnetic moment creates loss-cone distributions and temperature anisotropy, with gravitational filtering enhancing hot particle populations at coronal heights.
AI.motivation: To understand how magnetic field expansion affects the density and temperature structure of the weakly collisional solar corona, particularly the combined effects of gravitational filtering and magnetic moment conservation.
AI.method: Starting from the Vlasov equation for a stationary two-component plasma in an expanding magnetic flux tube, the authors derive analytical expressions for particle distribution functions, density profiles, and temperature components (parallel, perpendicular, total), incorporating gravity, self-electrostatic interactions, Pannekoek-Rosseland electric field, and magnetic moment conservation.
AI.result: Conservation of energy and magnetic moment produces a loss-cone distribution reducing density relative to the unmagnetized case. A single-temperature boundary condition leads to a parallel temperature maximum. Analytical scaling laws for its location and amplitude are derived and validated numerically. The anisotropy persists regardless of boundary temperature distribution. Gravitational filtering amplifies hot populations at coronal heights, further enhanced by magnetic moment conservation.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a fully analytical kinetic framework for understanding how magnetic-field expansion shapes density and temperature in weakly collisional stellar coronae, with implications for solar corona modeling.

title: Well-posedness of the mean field game master equation on Carnot tori
summary: We study the master equation for a second-order mean field game on Carnot tori, which means the generic player can move periodically only along admissible trajectories given by the family of vector fields generating the Carnot group. As examples of sub-Riemannian manifolds, Carnot groups represent a type of non-commutative groups characterized by stratified Lie algebra structures. In order to obtain the well-posedness of the master equation, we analyze the properties of its solution by investigating a degenerate mean field game system for which there exists an equivalent characterization with the master equation. The main part of this paper lies in leveraging the regularity properties of solutions to two classes of linear degenerate parabolic equations and a class of linear degenerate coupled systems to derive the existence of solutions to the master equation. The research in this paper is motivated by \cite{19CDLL,24MMM}.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the master equation for second-order mean field games on Carnot tori, proving well-posedness by leveraging regularity properties of degenerate parabolic equations and coupled systems.
AI.motivation: The research is motivated by prior work (cite{19CDLL, 24MMM}) and aims to establish well-posedness of the master equation for mean field games on sub-Riemannian manifolds (Carnot groups), which feature non-commutative stratified Lie algebra structures.
AI.method: The authors analyze a degenerate mean field game system that is equivalent to the master equation. They leverage regularity properties of solutions to two classes of linear degenerate parabolic equations and a class of linear degenerate coupled systems to derive existence of solutions.
AI.result: The paper proves the existence of solutions to the master equation by establishing regularity properties of the associated degenerate mean field game system on Carnot tori.
AI.conclusion: The master equation for second-order mean field games is well-posed on Carnot tori, extending mean field game theory to sub-Riemannian geometric settings with non-commutative group structures.

title: Machine learning based prediction of optical properties in two-dimensional Mo-W-S-Se-Te transition-metal dichalcogenide alloys through physics-informed sampling
summary: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) alloys provide a compositionally tunable platform for controlling the optical and electronic properties. However, systematic prediction of their dielectric response across multicomponent alloy spaces remains challenging owing to the combinatorial cost of first-principles calculations. In this work, we combined ab initio optical-property calculations with a tabular foundation-model regression to predict the real and imaginary components of the frequency-dependent dielectric function for Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys. A dataset of 99 alloy structures spanning binary, ternary, quaternary, and quinary compositions was generated using density functional theory (DFT). The resulting polarization-dependent dielectric spectra were used to train a tabular prior-fitted network (TabPFN) and evaluated against the conventional Extra Trees and XGBoost models. To accommodate the in-context capacity limit of TabPFN, we introduced a non-uniform, physics-informed energy subsampling strategy that concentrates sampling in the optically active region above the band gap, where interband absorption is strongest. Trained solely on quaternary alloys, our TabPFN reconstructed the dielectric spectra of held-out quaternary compositions with an R2 > 0.98 and a mean absolute error below 0.10 for all four dielectric components, outperforming both baselines while requiring no gradient-based training or hyperparameter tuning. Our model further predicted derived optical quantities, including refractive index, extinction coefficient, and absorption coefficient. Additionally, our model generalized in a zero-shot manner to binary, ternary, and quinary alloys absent from the training set, with quinary predictions achieving an R2 > 0.97.

AI.tldr: A tabular foundation model (TabPFN) trained on DFT-calculated dielectric spectra of quaternary TMD alloys (Mo-W-S-Se-Te) predicts frequency-dependent dielectric functions with R² > 0.98, generalizes zero-shot to binary, ternary, and quinary compositions, and outperforms Extra Trees and XGBoost without hyperparameter tuning.
AI.motivation: Systematic prediction of dielectric response across multicomponent TMD alloy spaces is challenging due to the combinatorial cost of first-principles calculations.
AI.method: DFT calculations on 99 TMD alloy structures → training TabPFN with physics-informed energy subsampling (focusing on interband absorption region) → evaluated against Extra Trees and XGBoost.
AI.result: TabPFN achieved R² > 0.98, MAE < 0.10 for quaternary predictions; zero-shot generalization to binary/ternary/quinary alloys with quinary R² > 0.97; outperformed baselines without gradient training or hyperparameter tuning.
AI.conclusion: TabPFN combined with physics-informed subsampling is a highly efficient and accurate method for predicting dielectric spectra across unexplored compositional spaces in TMD alloys.

title: On the Approximation of the Unitary Operator Group Associated with a Rotation Matrix and Its Applications to Abstract Hyperbolic Equations
comment: Initial version of the manuscript, comprising 22 pages in total, including the cover page and 25 references
summary: The solution of the Cauchy problem for homogeneous abstract hyperbolic equations, together with its derivative, admits a vector representation in terms of a unitary operator group associated with a rotation matrix. A rational approximation of this unitary group is constructed and shown to possess optimal fourth-order convergence. The order of convergence is determined in accordance with the smoothness scale. Based on this rational approximation, a two-layer semi-discrete scheme is constructed for the approximate solution of Cauchy problems for nonhomogeneous abstract hyperbolic equations in both the linear and semi-linear settings. The convergence properties of the scheme are examined in relation to the regularity of the solution.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a rational approximation of a unitary operator group for abstract hyperbolic equations, achieving optimal fourth-order convergence, and constructs a two-layer semi-discrete scheme for solving Cauchy problems in linear and semi-linear settings.
AI.motivation: To construct efficient and high-order numerical schemes for solving Cauchy problems for abstract hyperbolic equations, including nonhomogeneous and semi-linear cases.
AI.method: The authors use a vector representation of the solution and its derivative via a unitary operator group associated with a rotation matrix, then construct a rational approximation of this unitary group with fourth-order convergence.
AI.result: The rational approximation achieves optimal fourth-order convergence, and the two-layer semi-discrete scheme demonstrates convergence that depends on the regularity of the solution.
AI.conclusion: The proposed rational approximation and semi-discrete scheme provide an effective approach for solving abstract hyperbolic equations with provable convergence properties tied to solution smoothness.

title: Harnack inequality for double-phase functionals with Muckenhoupt-type growth functions
summary: We investigate a general class of variational integrals under a structural condition imposed on the double-phase function, recently introduced in~\cite{ADKO2026}. In this setting, the strong Harnack inequality for non-negative local quasi-minimizers is established via an appropriate De Giorgi-type iteration argument. Most notably, the proposed analytical approach in this paper provides a new perspective for deriving Harnack-type inequalities for more general variational functionals under a Muckenhoupt-type structural condition on the double-phase function, without relying on the classical coefficient-freezing strategy based on the Hölder continuity of the modulating coefficient and the balance condition on the growth exponents.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a strong Harnack inequality for quasi-minimizers of a general class of double-phase variational integrals using a De Giorgi-type iteration, offering a new approach that avoids traditional coefficient-freezing methods and applies to broader functionals under Muckenhoupt-type conditions.
AI.motivation: To extend Harnack-type inequalities to more general double-phase variational functionals without relying on classical assumptions such as Hölder continuity of the modulating coefficient or the balance condition on growth exponents.
AI.method: A De Giorgi-type iteration argument adapted to the structural condition imposed on the double-phase function, recently introduced in the cited work~\cite{ADKO2026}.
AI.result: The strong Harnack inequality for non-negative local quasi-minimizers is established under the given structural condition.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach offers a new perspective for deriving Harnack-type inequalities for more general variational functionals under Muckenhoupt-type structural conditions, avoiding the classical coefficient-freezing strategy.

title: Tailoring optical Schrödinger cat states via orientation-dependent high-harmonic generation in $\rm{H}_2^+$
summary: We theoretically demonstrate that the molecular orientation angle $θ$ provides a structurally intrinsic, continuously tunable control parameter for engineering optical Schrödinger cat states via high-harmonic generation (HHG) in H$_2^+$. Coupling time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations to the fully quantized HHG framework, we evaluate the Wigner functions of the post-selected harmonic-mode states under two complementary conditioning strategies. Conditioning on resonance-enhanced low-order harmonics exploits the complementary dipole selection rules of the $1σ_g\to1σ_u$ and $1σ_g\to1π_u$ transitions, driving a kitten-cat crossover whose direction is opposite in the two channels as $θ$ is varied. Conditioning on plateau harmonics instead exploits two-center destructive interference, producing a reentrant cat$\to$kitten$\to$cat transition controlled by the order-dependent interference angle $θ^*(q)$. In both cases the crossover is decoupled from the laser intensity, focal geometry, and molecular density, offering a degree of control with no counterpart in atomic targets.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the molecular orientation angle θ in H₂⁺ can serve as a tunable control parameter for engineering optical Schrödinger cat states via HHG, with two complementary conditioning strategies producing distinct cat-to-kitten transitions that are independent of laser intensity and other experimental variables.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that molecular orientation offers a structurally intrinsic, continuously tunable parameter for controlling quantum optical cat states in HHG, overcoming the limitations of atomic targets where such control is not available.
AI.method: The authors couple time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations to a fully quantized HHG framework, evaluating Wigner functions of post-selected harmonic-mode states under two conditioning strategies: (1) resonance-enhanced low-order harmonics exploiting dipole selection rules, and (2) plateau harmonics exploiting two-center destructive interference.
AI.result: Two complementary control mechanisms are identified: low-order harmonics produce a kitten-cat crossover with opposite direction in the two symmetry channels as θ varies; plateau harmonics yield a reentrant cat→kitten→cat transition controlled by the order-dependent interference angle θ*(q). Both transitions are decoupled from laser intensity, focal geometry, and molecular density.
AI.conclusion: Molecular orientation provides a unique, experimentally clean control knob for Schrödinger cat state engineering via HHG, with no counterpart in atomic systems, offering advantages for quantum optical applications.

title: An unfitted boundary algebraic equation method with Calderón preconditioning for 2D Stokes flow in irregular geometry
summary: We present an unfitted boundary algebraic equation method for the two-dimensional exterior/interior Stokes equations on a staggered MAC grid. By constructing an explicit free-space pair of velocity and pressure lattice Green's functions (LGFs) from free-space Laplace LGFs, we represent homogeneous fields using sources supported exclusively on thin staggered boundary layers. This formulation imposes physical Dirichlet data at cut points via local interpolation, while sampled-normal rank updates remove hydrostatic null modes associated with single or multiple obstacles. The workflow parallels that of classical boundary integral formulations and requires no artificial boundary conditions for exterior flows, but follows a discretize-then-represent route and does not require singular/near-singular quadrature. The resulting dense boundary system is solved via GMRES, utilizing a componentwise discrete Calderón preconditioner built from the scalar Laplace kernel and padded FFTs for fast volume convolutions. Extensive numerical validation, including multiply connected domains, narrow gaps, and Moffatt eddies, confirms discrete incompressibility to solver accuracy and recovers the expected Moffatt eddy scaling. We achieve second-order velocity and pressure convergence and bound maximum discrete divergence within numerical accuracy. The discrete Calderón preconditioner reduces the condition number by orders of magnitude and yields nearly mesh-independent conditioning in exterior configurations, while remaining effective---though more demanding---for narrow-gap and fine-grid interior problems.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an unfitted boundary algebraic equation method for 2D Stokes equations on staggered MAC grids, using free-space lattice Green's functions, boundary source layers, and a discrete Calderón preconditioner to achieve second-order convergence without artificial boundary conditions or singular quadrature.
