AI.motivation: To develop a numerical method for exterior/interior Stokes flows that avoids artificial boundary conditions (for exterior problems), singular/near-singular quadrature, and fitted meshes, while maintaining high accuracy and discrete incompressibility.
AI.method: The method constructs explicit free-space velocity-pressure lattice Green's functions from Laplace LGFs, represents fields via sources on thin staggered boundary layers, imposes Dirichlet data via local interpolation at cut points, removes hydrostatic null modes via rank updates, and solves the dense boundary system with GMRES using a componentwise discrete Calderón preconditioner built from scalar Laplace kernels and padded FFTs.
AI.result: Second-order velocity and pressure convergence, discrete incompressibility to solver accuracy, recovery of Moffatt eddy scaling, and orders-of-magnitude condition number reduction via the Calderón preconditioner, with nearly mesh-independent conditioning for exterior problems.
AI.conclusion: The unfitted boundary algebraic equation approach is effective for 2D Stokes flows on MAC grids, offering a clean parallel to classical boundary integral methods without quadrature difficulties, and works reliably across multiply connected domains, narrow gaps, and fine-grid interior problems.

title: Upper bound for the first $p$-Steklov eigenvalue in $\mathbb{R}^n$
summary: For $p\in(1,n]$ and any bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, we prove the sharp inequality \[ Λ_p(Ω):=\frac{W_p(Ω)}{P(Ω)V(Ω)^{p/n}}\geqω_n^{-p/n}, \qquad W_p(Ω)=\int_{\partialΩ}|x|^p\ dS, \] with equality holding exactly at centered balls. Combining this with the isoperimetric inequality yields the explicit upper bound \[ σ_{1,p}(Ω)\leq \frac{A(n,p)}{r(Ω^*)^{p-1}}, \] where $Ω^*$ is a ball having the same perimeter as $Ω$, and $A(n,p)=1$ for $1<p\leq 2$, $A(n,p)=n^{p/2-1}$ for $2<p\leq n$. When $p=2$, the result recovers the higher-dimensional Weinstock inequality of Bucur et al. [J. Differential Geom. 2021]. We also obtain an explicit upper bound for the first Wentzell eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian on convex domains.

AI.tldr: The paper proves a sharp geometric inequality for convex domains involving a weighted perimeter functional \(W_p(\Omega)\), shows it is minimized by centered balls, and uses it to derive explicit upper bounds for the first eigenvalue of the \(p\)-Laplacian (Steklov and Wentzell problems).
AI.motivation: To establish sharp inequalities linking geometric quantities (perimeter, volume, weighted surface integrals) for convex domains, and to obtain explicit eigenvalue bounds for the \(p\)-Laplacian, generalizing known results like the Weinstock inequality.
AI.method: The proof combines a sharp inequality \(\Lambda_p(\Omega) \ge \omega_n^{-p/n}\) with equality at centered balls, together with the classical isoperimetric inequality, to derive eigenvalue upper bounds. The constants \(A(n,p)\) depend on the range of \(p\).
AI.result: 1) Sharp inequality \(\Lambda_p(\Omega) \ge \omega_n^{-p/n}\) for \(p\in(1,n]\) on bounded convex domains, equality at centered balls. 2) Explicit upper bound \(\sigma_{1,p}(\Omega) \le A(n,p)/r(\Omega^*)^{p-1}\) where \(\Omega^*\) is a ball with same perimeter, with \(A(n,p)=1\) for \(1<p\le2\) and \(A(n,p)=n^{p/2-1}\) for \(2<p\le n\). 3) Explicit upper bound for the first Wentzell eigenvalue of the \(p\)-Laplacian.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides sharp geometric inequalities and explicit eigenvalue bounds for convex domains, recovering and generalizing known results (e.g., Weinstock inequality for \(p=2\)).

title: A general synthetic iterative solver for axisymmetric rarefied gas and electrostatic charged-particle flows
summary: An axisymmetric general synthetic iterative scheme (AxiGSIS) is proposed to simulate rarefied gas flows and charged particle transport under prescribed electrostatic fields. This solver adopts a finite-volume discrete velocity method defined over the two-dimensional axisymmetric meridian plane paired with a three dimensional molecular velocity space. Under the GSIS framework, the kinetic solver computes nonequilibrium stress and heat flux, which are subsequently imported as corrective source terms into the macroscopic synthetic system. Fast iterative updates of low order flow primitive variables are performed on this macroscopic system, whose corrected flow fields are then fed back to the kinetic solver. This bidirectional coupling enables rapid propagation of macroscopic information and substantially accelerates steady state convergence, particularly in near continuum flow regimes. Four benchmark flows are examined: the Taylor Couette flow, neutral nozzle expansion flow, charged particle flow past an electrostatic sphere, and electrostatically accelerated charged-particle nozzle flow. Results show that AxiGSIS reproduces the reference kinetic solutions and accurately captures axisymmetric flow physics and charged-particle responses to prescribed electrostatic fields. Utilizing fewer spatial cells and iteration steps, AxiGSIS substantially cuts computational overhead relative to conventional kinetic iterations, particularly for low and moderate Knudsen number flows.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes AxiGSIS, an axisymmetric general synthetic iterative scheme that couples a kinetic solver with a macroscopic synthetic system to efficiently simulate rarefied gas flows and charged particle transport under electrostatic fields, achieving faster convergence and lower computational cost compared to conventional methods.
AI.motivation: To accelerate steady-state convergence and reduce computational overhead in simulating axisymmetric rarefied gas flows and charged particle transport, which are computationally expensive with conventional kinetic solvers.
AI.method: AxiGSIS uses a finite-volume discrete velocity method on a 2D axisymmetric meridian plane with 3D molecular velocity space. It bidirectionally couples a kinetic solver (computing nonequilibrium stress/heat flux) and a macroscopic synthetic system (fast iterative updates of primitive variables with corrective source terms).
AI.result: AxiGSIS accurately reproduces reference kinetic solutions for four benchmark flows (Taylor-Couette flow, neutral nozzle expansion, charged particle flow past an electrostatic sphere, and electrostatically accelerated nozzle flow), with substantially fewer spatial cells and iteration steps, especially for low to moderate Knudsen numbers.
AI.conclusion: AxiGSIS effectively accelerates convergence and cuts computational overhead for axisymmetric rarefied/charged particle flows under electrostatic fields, making it a promising solver for near-continuum flow regimes.

title: 3D Uncertainty Quantification for the Photo-Acoustic Tomography
summary: Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) is a promising modality for high-resolution biomedical imaging, motivating the need for reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) of reconstructed images. Bayesian approaches provide a rigorous framework for UQ but remain computationally challenging for realistic three-dimensional PAT and are sensitive to numerical approximations in the governing wave equation. We develop a finite-element Bayesian UQ framework for PAT that accommodates complex computational domains and detector geometries while enabling large-scale three-dimensional inference. The proposed methodology reformulates the randomize-then-optimize (RTO) sampling strategy as a matrix-free algorithm that generates independent posterior samples using only forward and adjoint wave propagations. Particular attention is given to constructing an adjoint discretization that forms an exact transpose pair with the discrete forward operator while remaining consistent with the continuous PAT adjoint, enabling efficient least-squares solvers within the sampling procedure. We investigate the influence of temporal discretization, artificial boundary conditions, and adjoint consistency on posterior uncertainty and identify discretization strategies that avoid numerical artifacts. The framework is validated against exact posterior statistics, existing Bayesian PAT methods, and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), and is demonstrated on a three-dimensional problem with approximately $2\times 10^5$ unknowns on a general finite-element domain. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first large-scale Bayesian PAT study on general three-dimensional finite-element geometries, and the methodology extends naturally to a broad class of linear PDE-constrained inverse problems.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a scalable finite-element Bayesian uncertainty quantification framework for 3D photoacoustic tomography using a matrix-free randomize-then-optimize sampling method with adjoint-consistent discretization, validated on a problem with ~200K unknowns.
AI.motivation: PAT is promising for high-resolution imaging but lacks reliable UQ; existing Bayesian approaches are computationally prohibitive for realistic 3D problems and sensitive to numerical discretization artifacts.
AI.method: A matrix-free RTO sampling algorithm using only forward/adjoint wave propagations, with careful adjoint-consistent finite-element discretization and efficient least-squares solvers.
AI.result: Validated against exact posteriors, existing Bayesian PAT methods, and HMC/NUTS; demonstrated on a 3D finite-element domain with ~2×10^5 unknowns — the first large-scale Bayesian PAT study on general 3D geometries.
AI.conclusion: The framework is computationally feasible for large-scale 3D Bayesian PAT inference and extends naturally to other linear PDE-constrained inverse problems.

title: On the well-posedness of porous medium equations on general metric measure spaces
summary: We develop, on general metric measure spaces, a well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem of the signed porous medium equation and its fast diffusion counterpart \begin{equation*} \partial_t u=\mathcal{L}\left(|u|^{m-1}u\right), \qquad m>0, \end{equation*} where $\mathcal{L}$ is the generator of a symmetric Dirichlet form. We prove that, for every initial datum $u_0\in L^{m+1}(M,μ)$, there exists a unique function $u$ that weakly solves the equation in a suitable sense. The proof is based on the Rothe method and the theory of monotone operators and only uses the definition of the Dirichlet form and its extended version; no extra properties of the form or geometry of the space are needed. Consequently, the theory applies to a wide range of metric measure spaces, in particular, including non-smooth fractals.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a well-posedness theory for the signed porous medium equation and its fast diffusion counterpart on general metric measure spaces using the Rothe method and monotone operator theory, requiring only a symmetric Dirichlet form and thus applicable to non-smooth fractals.
AI.motivation: To establish existence and uniqueness of solutions for the signed porous medium equation on general metric measure spaces, including non-smooth fractals, without requiring extra geometric properties.
AI.method: The authors use the Rothe method (time discretization) combined with the theory of monotone operators, relying solely on the definition of a symmetric Dirichlet form and its extended version.
AI.result: For every initial datum u₀ ∈ L^{m+1}(M, μ), there exists a unique weak solution u to the equation ∂_t u = ℒ(|u|^{m-1}u) with m>0.
AI.conclusion: The theory applies to a wide range of metric measure spaces, including non-smooth fractals, demonstrating broad applicability beyond smooth settings.

title: Jordan algebras, hemiplex numbers, and the Cholesky decomposition of arbitrary symmetric matrices
comment: 17 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to the SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications. Software: https://github.com/timholy/HemiplexNumbers.jl and https://github.com/timholy/HemiplexFactorizations.jl
summary: Positive-semidefinite matrices are most efficiently factored using the Cholesky decomposition. For indefinite matrices, the Cholesky factorization does not exist, and the alternatives face greater challenges in achieving numeric stability and preservation of banded structure. Here we pursue an analogy between the requirement for positive-semidefinite matrices and the solution of the quadratic equation x^2 = c for c <= 0. It is shown that a non-associative algebra, called the hemiplex numbers, allows the Cholesky factorization to be computed for arbitrary symmetric matrices. Crucially, the hemiplex Cholesky factorization does not require pivoting for its existence or stability, allowing it to preserve banded structure. For singular matrices it produces a parametrization of the null space, and provides opportunity for truncation of nearly-null directions in a manner similar to common usage of the singular value decomposition. The hemiplex Cholesky factorization may be a practically useful addition to the tools for solving symmetric linear equations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the hemiplex Cholesky factorization, which extends the classic Cholesky decomposition to indefinite symmetric matrices using a non-associative algebra (hemiplex numbers), enabling pivot-free, banded-structure-preserving factorization with null-space parametrization and truncation capabilities.
AI.motivation: Standard Cholesky decomposition only works for positive-semidefinite matrices. For indefinite matrices, existing alternatives struggle with numeric stability and preserving banded structure, motivating the need for a new approach.
AI.method: The method draws an analogy between positive-semidefinite matrix requirements and solving x^2 = c for c ≤ 0. It introduces the hemiplex numbers (a non-associative algebra) to compute Cholesky factorization for arbitrary symmetric matrices without pivoting.
AI.result: The hemiplex Cholesky factorization does not require pivoting for existence or stability, thus preserving banded structure. For singular matrices, it parametrizes the null space and allows truncation of nearly-null directions akin to SVD.
AI.conclusion: The hemiplex Cholesky factorization may be a practically useful addition to the tools for solving symmetric linear equations, offering advantages for indefinite and singular systems.

title: An inverse coefficient problem for a semilinear wave equation by the first order linearization
summary: This paper investigates recovery of an unknown coefficient in a semilinear wave equation defined on a bounded, open, and strictly convex domain in \(\mathbb{R}^{1+n}\) with \(n \ge 2\). We demonstrate that the unknown coefficient \(q\) appearing in the semilinear wave equation \(\square u + q u^m = 0\) with Neumann boundary conditions can be reconstructed with Hölder stability from the linearized Neumann-to-Dirichlet (NtD) map. Our approach combines first-order linearization with the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion (PIE) identity, and employs geometric optics solutions for wave equations in two distinct regimes: the case \(m=2\) with \(q = q(x)\), and the case \(m \ge 3\) with \(q = q(t,x)\). Furthermore, numerical examples illustrate that the unknown coefficient can also be effectively reconstructed using a neural network-based inversion algorithm within the framework of the least squares method.

AI.tldr: This paper shows Hölder stability for recovering an unknown coefficient in a semilinear wave equation from the linearized Neumann-to-Dirichlet map using linearization, the PIE identity, and geometric optics solutions, with numerical validation via neural networks.
AI.motivation: To establish stable reconstruction of an unknown coefficient in semilinear wave equations, which is an inverse problem with applications in imaging and parameter identification.
AI.method: Combines first-order linearization with the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion (PIE) identity, uses geometric optics solutions for wave equations, and applies neural network-based inversion with least squares.
AI.result: Hölder stability is achieved for reconstructing q(x) when m=2 and q(t,x) when m≥3 from the linearized NtD map; numerical examples demonstrate effective reconstruction via neural networks.
AI.conclusion: The unknown coefficient in semilinear wave equations can be stably recovered from linearized boundary data, with both theoretical stability guarantees and practical numerical validation.

title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
summary: Density functional theory (DFT) serves as a reliable tool for atomistic molecular simulations, while machine learning potentials have become powerful complements to balance accuracy and efficiency. In this work, we release OpenGEM26 (Open Generated Ensemble of Molecules, 2026), a large-scale dataset comprising 200,000 unique molecules and 4.4 million conformations composed of H, C, N, O, S and Cl with up to ten heavy atoms. All calculations are carried out at the ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP levels with dispersion corrections, and complete structural optimization trajectories and abundant non-equilibrium structures are recorded. Statistical analyses confirm that this dataset covers a broader conformational space than QM9 in terms of energy, bond lengths and bond angles. A graph neural network-based potential GPTFF-mol is trained using the new dataset, achieving an energy mean absolute error of 16 meV/molecule, which is equivalent to 0.82meV/atom, and superior force prediction performance compared with ANI-2x. Validated by butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization tests, the model accurately describes molecular dynamical behaviors and reaction barriers at distorted geometries. This work provides a high-quality resource and robust ML potential for efficient simulations of sulfur- and chlorine-containing organic molecules.

AI.tldr: OpenGEM26 dataset (200K molecules, 4.4M conformations of H/C/N/O/S/Cl) with DFT calculations at ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP/TZVP levels is released. A GNN potential GPTFF-mol trained on it achieves 16 meV/molecule energy MAE and outperforms ANI-2x in force prediction.
AI.motivation: Existing datasets like QM9 lack sufficient conformational diversity for S/Cl-containing molecules. There is a need for high-quality DFT data covering broader conformational space to train accurate and efficient machine learning potentials.
AI.method: OpenGEM26 dataset: 200K molecules, 4.4M conformations (H, C, N, O, S, Cl, ≤10 heavy atoms). DFT at ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP & Def2-TZVP with dispersion corrections. GPTFF-mol: graph neural network potential trained on this dataset.
AI.result: Energy MAE = 16 meV/molecule (0.82 meV/atom); superior force prediction vs ANI-2x. Validated on butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization, accurately describing dynamics and reaction barriers.
AI.conclusion: OpenGEM26 provides a high-quality resource for S/Cl-containing organic molecules, and GPTFF-mol offers a robust ML potential for efficient simulations of distorted geometries.

title: librla: Randomized Linear Algebra Library
summary: The library \texttt{librla} is a randomized linear algebra library that is specifically designed for the intermediate-sized matrices (of dimension up to roughly 10,000) that arise in applications such as reduced order modeling, fast direct solvers, least squares solves and, in some settings, data compression. \texttt{librla} is the first software package that is both stable and efficient in several high-level languages: MATLAB, Python and Julia. It also provides increased functionality over existing software. Specifically, it allows the user to choose to create a factorization based on a fixed rank or a desired tolerance. The factorization options include QR, SVD and the interpolative decomposition. Additionally, the factorization can be generated either with access to the matrix or access to a matrix-vector multiplication routine. Numerical results compare the Python implementation with the available PyTorch and SciPy randomized factorizations. Performance of \texttt{librla} in the three languages is comparable.

AI.tldr: Librla is a randomized linear algebra library for intermediate-sized matrices (up to ~10,000 dimensions) supporting QR, SVD, and interpolative decomposition in MATLAB, Python, and Julia, with options for fixed rank or tolerance-based factorization.
AI.motivation: To provide a stable and efficient randomized linear algebra library across multiple high-level languages (MATLAB, Python, Julia) for intermediate-sized matrices, filling the gap in existing software that lacks cross-language support or sufficient functionality.
AI.method: The library implements randomized factorizations (QR, SVD, interpolative decomposition) with two modes: fixed rank or tolerance-based. Supports two access patterns: direct matrix access or matrix-vector multiplication routines.
AI.result: Python implementation was compared against PyTorch and SciPy randomized factorizations. Performance across MATLAB, Python, and Julia is comparable.
AI.conclusion: Librla offers a unique combination of cross-language stability, efficiency, and flexible factorization options (rank/tolerance, access patterns) for intermediate-scale linear algebra problems.

title: Liouville Rigidity for Real and Complex Degenerate Hessian Equations
summary:
We prove Liouville rigidity theorems for translation-invariant real and complex Hessian equations in the viscosity sense, where the PDE is encoded by an admissible set $\mathcal{A}$. The main structural notion is Liouville admissibility, a recursive geometric condition requiring each quotient set to be either boundary compatible or to fall into a terminal class. Our main theorem states that every bounded, globally $C^{0,α}$ entire viscosity solution of \[ \mathrm{Hess}_{\mathbb F}u\in\partial\mathcal{A} \]
  is constant if and only if $\mathcal{A}$ is Liouville admissible; thus the Liouville-type property is characterized as a geometric property of the admissible set.
  A central class of examples arises from polarizations of univariate Gårding polynomials satisfying the monotone root sequence condition, producing mixed elementary-symmetric admissible sets and recovering the standard $k$-Hessian equations as monomial cases. The framework also allows anisotropic constructions, including linear pullbacks and intersections of admissible sets.

AI.tldr: Proves that bounded viscosity solutions to translation-invariant Hessian equations are constant iff the admissible set satisfies a recursive geometric condition called Liouville admissibility.
AI.motivation: To characterize when Liouville-type theorems (all bounded entire solutions are constant) hold for general Hessian equations governed by admissible sets, extending beyond classical k-Hessian cases.
AI.method: Introduces the notion of "Liouville admissibility" — a recursive geometric condition requiring each quotient set to be boundary compatible or in a terminal class. Uses viscosity solution techniques and PDE geometry.
AI.result: A bounded, globally C^{0,α} entire viscosity solution of Hess_F u ∈ ∂A is constant iff A is Liouville admissible. Includes constructions via Gårding polynomials with monotone root sequences, mixed elementary-symmetric sets, and anisotropic admissible sets.
AI.conclusion: The Liouville property for Hessian equations is fully characterized as a geometric property of the admissible set, unifying and generalizing known results (e.g., k-Hessian equations).

title: Structure-Preserving Spectral Dynamic Programming on Compact Lie Groups
summary: We study spectral approximations of the dynamic programming semigroup for finite-horizon optimal control on a connected compact Lie group $G$, and of the associated first-order Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. The Bellman operator is monotone and non-expansive in the supremum norm, while the Peter-Weyl decomposition of $L^{2}(G)$, on which every Fourier method on $G$ rests, is orthogonal, and the mismatch is quantitative. The natural sup-norm error recursion of the Galerkin iteration is amplified at every step by the Lebesgue constant of the spectral projection, which grows logarithmically on $S^{1}$ and polynomially on compact Lie groups of rank one, including $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, and in computation the iteration violates elementary bounds within a few steps. We restore the dynamic programming structure at the discrete level by replacing the orthogonal projection with spectral filters of Markov type. An auxiliary heat-kernel/vanishing-viscosity scheme yields qualitative sup-norm convergence for Lipschitz data. The main result is a Fejér-type filter on $G$, finite-rank, positivity preserving and non-expansive, together with a convergence theorem at the rate $O(\sqrtδ+\sqrt{ε+1/(δN^2)})$ for Lipschitz data, where $δ$ is the time step, $N$ the spectral resolution and $ε$ the viscosity. The viscosity may be zero, and the coupling $δ=N^{-1}$ then gives the rate $N^{-1/2}$. The proof interprets the filter as a small random perturbation of the controlled dynamics, requires neither a priori regularity of the value function nor a consistency argument in the viscosity sense for the filtering step, and extends to a fully discrete realization based on positive cubature, with exact Wigner transport on $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates and filter bias and quantify the frame dependence of two chart-based baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper develops spectral approximation methods for dynamic programming on compact Lie groups, using Markov-type spectral filters to overcome divergence issues caused by mismatched norms (sup-norm vs L2), achieving convergence rates of O(√δ + √(ε + 1/(δN²))) with Fejér-type filters.
AI.motivation: Standard Fourier/Galerkin methods fail for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on Lie groups because the Bellman operator is sup-norm non-expansive while Peter-Weyl decomposition is L2-orthogonal, causing error amplification via Lebesgue constants that grows logarithmically on S¹ and polynomially on rank-one groups like SO(3).
AI.method: Replace orthogonal spectral projection with positivity-preserving, non-expansive Fejér-type Markov filters; introduce an auxiliary heat-kernel/viscosity scheme; use a probabilistic interpretation (small random perturbation of controlled dynamics) to prove convergence without requiring a priori regularity or viscosity consistency.
AI.result: Convergence rate O(√δ + √(ε + 1/(δN²))) for Lipschitz data, which becomes O(N^{-1/2}) when δ = N^{-1} and ε = 0. Numerical experiments on SO(3) confirm predicted rates and filter bias, showing superiority over chart-based baselines.
AI.conclusion: Spectral filters of Markov type restore dynamic programming structure at the discrete level and provide provably convergent approximations, enabling practical computation on compact Lie groups like SO(3).

title: The mean-field limit of non-exchangeable particle systems with non-conservative dynamics and adaptive weights
summary: In the paper we introduce vector-valued dynamic extended graphons in order to obtain the mean-filed limit for certain class of problems with adaptive weights. We impose fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections, which allows us to cover the case of sparse graphs.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces vector-valued dynamic extended graphons to derive mean-field limits for problems with adaptive weights under general assumptions, including sparse graphs.
AI.motivation: To obtain mean-field limits for problems involving adaptive weights, particularly for sparse graphs which require more general assumptions on initial connection matrices.
AI.method: Introduces vector-valued dynamic extended graphons as a mathematical framework to model adaptive weights and derive mean-field limits.
AI.result: The method successfully covers the case of sparse graphs under fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections.
AI.conclusion: Vector-valued dynamic extended graphons provide a viable approach for mean-field limits in adaptive weight problems, extending to sparse graph scenarios.

title: Rigidity of weak solutions for anisotropic N-Laplacian equation with Neumann or Robin boundary condition
summary: This paper is devoted to the rigidity of weak solutions for anisotropic $N$-Laplacian equations with Neumann or Robin boundary conditions on smooth bounded convex domains of $\mathbb{R}^N$. The anisotropic operator is given by $$a(ξ) = H^{N-1}(ξ)\nabla H(ξ),$$ where $H$ stands for a norm on $\mathbb{R}^N$; this formulation contains the classical $N$-Laplacian as a special case. We establish a key integral inequality involving the anisotropic gradient and the second fundamental form of the domain boundary, which acts as the core technical tool in our proofs. Under natural monotonicity assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove that all weak solutions to the Neumann boundary problem are constant, without requiring any a priori boundedness assumption on the solution. Furthermore, we extend this rigidity result to Robin boundary value problems by imposing suitable constraints on the boundary nonlinear term. Moreover, our rigidity results remain valid not only on bounded convex domains but also on suitable unbounded domains. By working under substantially weaker assumptions than those previously available, we establish rigidity results that fill the gaps in the existing literature for anisotropic $N$-Laplacian equations with nonlinear boundary conditions and substantially extend the rigidity theory of anisotropic quasilinear elliptic equations at the critical exponent $p=N$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that weak solutions to anisotropic N-Laplacian equations with Neumann or Robin boundary conditions on convex domains are necessarily constant, under weak assumptions, using a novel integral inequality.
AI.motivation: To establish rigidity (i.e., that all weak solutions are constant) for anisotropic N-Laplacian equations with nonlinear boundary conditions, filling gaps in existing literature by working under substantially weaker assumptions than previously available.
AI.method: The authors derive a key integral inequality involving the anisotropic gradient and the second fundamental form of the domain boundary. This inequality serves as the core technical tool to prove rigidity for Neumann and Robin boundary problems under natural monotonicity assumptions, without requiring a priori boundedness of solutions.
AI.result: All weak solutions to the anisotropic N-Laplacian Neumann problem are constant under natural monotonicity assumptions. This rigidity extends to Robin boundary problems with suitable constraints on the boundary nonlinear term. Results hold on both bounded convex domains and suitable unbounded domains.
AI.conclusion: The paper significantly extends the rigidity theory for anisotropic quasilinear elliptic equations at the critical exponent p=N, filling gaps in existing literature with weaker assumptions.

title: Bayesian optimization approach for tracking a moving target from far-field data in three dimensions
summary: We investigate a three-dimensional inverse scattering problem for tracking a rigidly moving target from far-field data generated by a single incident field. Extending our recent two-dimensional study, we develop a Bayesian optimization framework for simultaneously tracking the target's location and orientation over successive time steps, with the translational and rotational motions modeled as independent stochastic processes. We derive analytical formulas for the far-field pattern under translations and rotations and use them to design a Bayesian optimization procedure tailored to the tracking problem. We further establish posterior consistency for the underlying probabilistic model. When the target shape is unknown, its shape is identified at the initial time using a fully connected neural network trained on a precomputed dataset. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

AI.tldr: The paper extends a 2D inverse scattering framework to 3D for tracking a rigidly moving target's position and orientation using far-field data from a single incident field, employing Bayesian optimization with stochastic motion models, deriving analytical far-field formulas, proving posterior consistency, and using a neural network for unknown shape identification.
AI.motivation: To solve the 3D inverse scattering problem of tracking a rigidly moving target's location and orientation over time from far-field data generated by a single incident field.
AI.method: Bayesian optimization framework with independent stochastic processes for translational and rotational motion; analytical far-field formulas under motion; fully connected neural network for unknown shape identification at initial time.
AI.result: Posterior consistency is established for the probabilistic model; numerical experiments validate the framework's effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The proposed 3D Bayesian optimization-based tracking approach works effectively for both known and unknown target shapes, with theoretical guarantees on posterior consistency.

title: Global bifurcation for steady viscous roll waves on an incline
summary: We construct a branch of travelling periodic `roll wave' solutions to the free-boundary incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on an inclined plane in two dimensions. These solutions bifurcate from a parallel shear flow, under natural assumptions on the related Orr--Sommerfeld equation. Using techniques from analytic global bifurcation theory, we extend the local branch to a global curve of solutions. A key step of the proof is reformulating the problem, including the unknown free boundary, as an elliptic system in the sense of Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg. Finally, we verify the hypotheses on the Orr--Sommerfeld equation for two regimes: small wavenumber and low Reynolds number.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs travelling periodic "roll wave" solutions to the 2D free-boundary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on an inclined plane, bifurcating from parallel shear flow using global bifurcation theory.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish the existence of roll wave solutions (a type of free-surface flow) and extend the local bifurcation branch to a global solution curve, with verification for small wavenumber and low Reynolds number regimes.
AI.method: Reformulates the problem (including the unknown free boundary) as an elliptic system in the Agmon-Douglis-Nirenberg sense, then applies analytic global bifurcation theory to extend local branches to global curves.
AI.result: Constructs a global curve of travelling periodic roll wave solutions bifurcating from parallel shear flow, and verifies the Orr-Sommerfeld equation hypotheses for two regimes: small wavenumber and low Reynolds number.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous global bifurcation analysis for roll wave solutions in free-boundary Navier-Stokes, with verified conditions for physically relevant parameter regimes.

title: Global existence and boundedness for a degenerate chemotaxis system with indirect signal production via minimizing movement schemes
summary: Global existence and boundedness of weak solutions for a fully parabolic degenerate chemotaxis system with indirect signal production are proved for any initial data in the subcritical case and under smallness conditions in the critical and supercritical cases. To construct weak solutions, a time discrete scheme is set up, for which the first equation has a gradient flow structure with respect to the 2-Wasserstein distance, while the other two equations feature an L\textsuperscript{2}-variational structure. The proof relies in particular on the flow interchange method and discrete maximal regularity.

AI.tldr: The paper proves global existence and boundedness of weak solutions for a fully parabolic degenerate chemotaxis system with indirect signal production under various conditions using a time-discrete scheme with gradient flow and variational structures.
AI.motivation: To establish global existence and boundedness results for weak solutions of a degenerate chemotaxis system with indirect signal production, addressing subcritical, critical, and supercritical cases.
AI.method: A time-discrete scheme is constructed where the first equation has a gradient flow structure w.r.t. 2-Wasserstein distance, and the other two equations have an L²-variational structure. The proof uses the flow interchange method and discrete maximal regularity.
AI.result: Global existence and boundedness of weak solutions are proved for any initial data in the subcritical case, and under smallness conditions in the critical and supercritical cases.
AI.conclusion: The proposed time-discrete approach successfully handles the degenerate chemotaxis system with indirect signal production, establishing existence and boundedness across different parameter regimes.

title: Neutral curves and traveling waves in plane Poiseuille flow
summary: We study the spectrum of the Orr--Sommerfeld operator associated with the incompressible plane Poiseuille flow in the high-Reynolds-number regime. In the Tollmien--Schlichting eigenvalue region, we prove the existence and uniqueness of the lower and upper branches of the neutral curve. For each sufficiently small fixed wavenumber $α$, the viscosities corresponding to the lower and upper neutral branches satisfy $ν\sim |α|^7$ and $ν\sim |α|^{11}$, respectively. Equivalently, for each sufficiently small viscosity $ν$, the corresponding lower and upper neutral wavenumbers satisfy $α^2\sim ν^{2/7}$ and $α^2\sim ν^{2/11}$, respectively. We also establish the simplicity of the neutral eigenvalues and verify the transversal crossing condition on both neutral branches. The proof is based on a boundary-adapted version of the Rayleigh--Airy iteration scheme, together with precise expansions and refined estimates for the correction terms and their parameter derivatives. These spectral results verify the assumptions required in the classical Hopf bifurcation framework of Joseph--Sattinger \cite{JS1972} and Iooss \cite{Iooss1972}, and hence yield traveling-wave solutions bifurcating from the plane Poiseuille flow at the neutral points.

AI.tldr: This paper rigorously analyzes the Orr-Sommerfeld operator for plane Poiseuille flow at high Reynolds numbers, proving existence and uniqueness of lower/upper neutral branches (with scalings ν~|α|⁷ and ν~|α|¹¹), establishing simplicity of neutral eigenvalues and transversal crossing, and thereby justifying Hopf bifurcation to traveling waves.
AI.motivation: To provide rigorous spectral analysis of the Orr-Sommerfeld operator in the high-Reynolds-number regime, verifying the assumptions needed for the classical Hopf bifurcation framework (Joseph-Sattinger, Iooss) to yield traveling-wave solutions bifurcating from plane Poiseuille flow at neutral points.
AI.method: A boundary-adapted Rayleigh-Airy iteration scheme, combined with precise asymptotic expansions and refined estimates for correction terms and their parameter derivatives.
AI.result: Proved existence and uniqueness of lower/upper neutral branches with scaling laws ν~|α|⁷ (lower) and ν~|α|¹¹ (upper); equivalently α²~ν^{2/7} and α²~ν^{2/11}. Established simplicity of neutral eigenvalues and verified the transversal crossing condition on both branches.
AI.conclusion: The spectral results validate the assumptions of the Joseph-Sattinger and Iooss Hopf bifurcation framework, thereby guaranteeing traveling-wave solutions bifurcating from plane Poiseuille flow at the neutral points.

title: An $L^p$-theory for global weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains
summary: In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes initial boundary value problem in exterior domains with initial data in the Lebesgue space $L^p$, $p\in (2,3)$, and show the existence of a global weak solution. For the quoted solution, we also furnish a structure theorem. In particular, we see that the weak solution becomes regular after a certain instant of time and it is also regular a. e. in time. Although a general $L^p$-theory for local strong/mild solutions is well-established in the literature, a corresponding theory for global weak solutions in exterior domains seems to be new. Of course, our results hold in the particular cases of the Cauchy problem and the initial boundary value problem in a half-space.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the existence of global weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains for initial data in L^p (2<p<3), and shows these solutions become regular after a certain time and are regular almost everywhere in time.
AI.motivation: To establish a global weak solution theory for the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains with L^p initial data (2<p<3), which was missing despite the existence of local strong/mild solution theories.
AI.method: The authors consider the Navier-Stokes initial boundary value problem in exterior domains with initial data in L^p (p∈(2,3)) and provide existence results alongside a structure theorem.
AI.result: Existence of global weak solutions is shown. These solutions become regular after a certain instant and are regular almost everywhere in time. Results also hold for the Cauchy problem and half-space cases.
AI.conclusion: A new global weak solution theory for Navier-Stokes in exterior domains is established, complementing the existing local strong/mild solution theories.

title: Magnetic relaxation for the MHD equations via the stable manifold method
summary: We prove that given any sufficiently small and regular solution $B$ of the stationary Euler equations there exists an infinite dimensional family of solutions $(u,b)$ of the non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics equations (MHD) that relax to $(0, B)$. More precisely, $(u,b) \to (0, B)$ exponentially fast as $t \to +\infty$. This family may be viewed as lying in the stable manifold of the non-resistive MHD equations around the equilibrium state $(0, B)$. The problem whether it actually coincides with the stable manifold remains open. As a byproduct of our result, we provide a large class of global regular solutions of the non-resistive MHD equations. Another consequence is that any sufficiently small and regular solution of the stationary Euler equation is (non-trivially) topologically accessible via MHD from a large class of magnetic fields according to the definition of Moffatt and, in this scenario, the topology of the magnetic lines is (entirely) preserved in the limit $t \to + \infty$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that small stationary Euler solutions B can be realized as asymptotic limits of infinite-dimensional families of non-resistive MHD solutions (u,b) that decay exponentially to (0,B), establishing stable manifold structure and topological accessibility.
AI.motivation: To understand the asymptotic behavior and stability of non-resistive MHD equations near equilibrium states, and to connect stationary Euler solutions with MHD dynamics through topological accessibility.
AI.method: The authors construct an infinite-dimensional family of MHD solutions that relax to (0,B) exponentially fast, using stable manifold techniques around the equilibrium (0,B) for the non-resistive MHD system.
AI.result: (1) Existence of infinite-dimensional families of global regular MHD solutions converging exponentially to (0,B); (2) Connection between stationary Euler solutions and MHD via topological accessibility; (3) Magnetic topology is entirely preserved in the t→∞ limit.
AI.conclusion: Small regular stationary Euler solutions are topologically accessible via non-resistive MHD, with magnetic line topology fully preserved in the limit, though whether the constructed family equals the full stable manifold remains open.

title: Double screening in the training dynamics of variational physics-informed neural networks for heterogeneous coupled parabolic systems
summary: We analyze the training dynamics of variational physics-informed neural networks applied to linear coupled parabolic convection--diffusion--reaction systems, called heterogeneous when only a subset of the components undergoes convective transport. In the neural tangent kernel regime, the gradient flow on the space-time variational residuals reduces to a linear differential system whose operator is a Gram matrix built from the space-time symbol of the system operator and the matrix tangent kernel. The main result is a double screening theorem. Under dominant convection, the Schur complement of this matrix relative to the block of convective components converges to an expression that involves only the diffusive block of the symbol, with no coupling term, together with the Schur complement of the tangent kernel. From this we derive four consequences, namely an exact identity quantifying the screened coupling energy, a degradation law for the training rate governed by the canonical correlations of the kernel, a bound on the condition number in terms of the Péclet number, and the non-participation of temporal frequencies in the screening mechanism. The growth of the condition number slows down shared-step gradient descent, whereas the continuous flow suffers no slowdown, which makes the training difficulty attributable to the optimizer rather than to the approximation. We finally show that the Adam optimizer, through its adaptive scaling, mitigates this difficulty provided that the architecture separates the parameters associated with the convective and diffusive components, confirming the architectural prescription that follows from the second screening. The predictions are validated numerically down to machine precision, on a two-dimensional exchanger, and by the full training of finite-width networks.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes training dynamics of variational physics-informed neural networks (VPINNs) for linear coupled parabolic convection-diffusion-reaction systems, proving a double screening theorem that shows how convective and diffusive components decouple under dominant convection, leading to condition number growth that slows gradient descent but not continuous flow, with Adam optimizer mitigating this issue through architectural separation.
AI.motivation: To understand why training physics-informed neural networks for convection-dominated problems is difficult, and to identify whether the difficulty stems from approximation capacity or from the optimizer.
AI.method: Neural tangent kernel (NTK) analysis of gradient flow on space-time variational residuals for VPINNs applied to heterogeneous coupled parabolic convection-diffusion-reaction systems, leading to a double screening theorem via Schur complement analysis.
AI.result: Double screening theorem showing decoupling of convective and diffusive components under dominant convection; identity for screened coupling energy; degradation law for training rate governed by canonical correlations; condition number bound growing with Péclet number; demonstration that Adam with architecturally separated parameters mitigates optimization difficulty.
AI.conclusion: Training difficulty in convection-dominated VPINNs is attributable to the optimizer (not approximation), and can be mitigated by Adam with architectural separation of convective and diffusive parameters.

title: A free boundary problem driven by boundary distance in the coincidence set
summary: We study a free boundary problem of minimising a functional containing a non-local term rewarding depth into the zero phase: for $u\ge0$ on a bounded, open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, we minimise $$J(u) = \int_Ω\left(\frac12|\nabla u|^2 - fu\right) \;-\; \int_{\{u=0\}} F\big(\mathrm{dist}(x,\partial \{u=0\})\big)\;\mathrm{d}x.$$ This kind of functional arises for example from a two-membranes problem with an adhesive contact energy. We first address a well-definedness issue caused by the non-local, boundary-sensitive nature of the functional and prove existence of minimisers, establishing along the way a weak lower semicontinuity result for the non-local term. We then derive stationarity conditions for minimisers, including a variational (Euler--Lagrange type) inequality, a PDE on the positivity set, and, under a mild non-degeneracy assumption, a free boundary condition obtained via inner variations and a Danskin-type differentiation of the distance function.

AI.tldr: The paper studies a free boundary problem with a non-local term rewarding depth into the zero phase, proving existence of minimizers and deriving stationarity conditions including a variational inequality, PDE, and free boundary condition via inner variations and Danskin-type differentiation.
AI.motivation: The functional arises from a two-membranes problem with adhesive contact energy, motivating the need to handle the non-local, boundary-sensitive term.
AI.method: Existence via weak lower semicontinuity of the non-local term; stationarity via variational inequality, PDE on the positivity set, and inner variations with Danskin-type differentiation under a non-degeneracy assumption.
AI.result: Proved existence of minimizers and derived stationarity conditions including a free boundary condition.
AI.conclusion: The non-local term is well-defined and minimizers satisfy refined stationarity conditions, advancing the theory for adhesive contact problems.

title: Sharp One-bubble Critical-Point Stability and Global Compactness for the Sobolev Trace Inequality
summary: Let $n\ge3$ and $1<p<n$. We first prove the local trace analogue of the sharp one-bubble critical-point stability theorem of Liu and Zhang~\cite{LiuZhang2025}: near a positive trace-bubble, the Euler--Lagrange residual controls the gradient distance to the normalized trace-bubble manifold with the sharp power $\max\{1,p-1\}$. Then, we establish a Struwe-type compactness theorem for the critical trace functional, which gives the trace counterpart of the Mercuri--Willem decomposition~\cite{MercuriWillem2010}. Combining Struwe-type compactness with the local stability estimate yields a sharp quantitative one-bubble critical-point stability theorem.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes sharp quantitative stability for trace Sobolev inequalities on bounded domains, proving a local stability estimate near positive trace-bubbles and a Struwe-type compactness theorem, which together yield a global one-bubble critical-point stability theorem.
AI.motivation: To extend the local and global stability results of Liu & Zhang (2025) and the decomposition of Mercuri & Willem (2010) from the Sobolev setting to the trace Sobolev inequality setting on bounded domains.
AI.method: Combines a local sharp stability estimate near normalized trace-bubbles (where the Euler-Lagrange residual controls the gradient distance with optimal power max{1, p-1}) with a Struwe-type compactness theorem for the critical trace functional, which serves as the trace analogue of the Mercuri-Willem decomposition.
AI.result: Proves the local trace analogue of the one-bubble critical-point stability theorem, establishes a trace counterpart of the Mercuri-Willem decomposition, and obtains a sharp quantitative one-bubble critical-point stability theorem for the trace Sobolev inequality.
AI.conclusion: The sharp quantitative stability for trace Sobolev inequalities is achieved by combining local stability estimates with compactness/decomposition arguments, mirroring the Sobolev case results.

title: Evolution of viscous vortex filaments and soliton-type propagation
summary:
We study the evolution of a viscous incompressible fluid whose initial vorticity is supported on a smooth open curve. We show that, for $νt\ll 1$ and sufficiently small Reynolds number $Γ/ν$, the vorticity is described at leading order by a Lamb--Oseen type vortex concentrated around a curve evolving according to the binormal flow predicted by the localized induction approximation. The solution is written as an explicit leading-order profile plus a lower-order perturbation, which is controlled in a Morrey $\mathcal{M}^{\infty}$ norm.
  Then, we apply this construction to the Hasimoto soliton. In this case, the estimates are uniform with respect to the torsion parameter, allowing us to consider a large-torsion regime in which the soliton undergoes a macroscopic displacement. We show that the corresponding Navier--Stokes solution contains a localized portion of the kinetic-energy distribution, associated with the binormal velocity, which remains concentrated inside a moving physical region and undergoes an order-one displacement during an admissible time interval.

AI.tldr: This paper rigorously shows that for small viscosity-times and low Reynolds numbers, the vorticity of a viscous fluid initially supported on a smooth curve is well-approximated by a Lamb-Oseen vortex evolving via the binormal flow (localized induction approximation). The construction is applied to the Hasimoto soliton, with uniform estimates enabling a large-torsion regime where the soliton undergoes macroscopic displacement while keeping kinetic energy concentrated.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous mathematical justification for the localized induction approximation (LIA) as a model for vortex filament dynamics in viscous incompressible fluids, and to demonstrate that the Hasimoto soliton (a solution of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation derived from LIA) corresponds to a real physical motion of concentrated vorticity in Navier-Stokes flow over admissible time intervals.
AI.method: The authors construct explicit leading-order Lamb-Oseen type vortex profiles around a curve evolving by binormal flow, then control lower-order perturbations using Morrey $\mathcal{M}^{\infty}$ norms under small Reynolds number $Γ/ν$ and $νt\ll1$ conditions. This framework is then applied to the Hasimoto soliton with uniform estimates in the torsion parameter.
AI.result: For $νt\ll1$ and sufficiently small $Γ/ν$, the vorticity is described at leading order by a Lamb-Oseen vortex concentrated around a curve evolving via binormal flow. For the Hasimoto soliton, estimates are uniform with respect to torsion, allowing a large-torsion regime where the soliton undergoes macroscopic (order-one) displacement, and the corresponding Navier-Stokes solution contains a localized kinetic-energy portion that remains concentrated and moves with the binormal velocity.
AI.conclusion: The localized induction approximation is rigorously validated as a leading-order description of viscous vortex filament dynamics in the small-time, low-Reynolds-number regime. The Hasimoto soliton is shown to correspond to a physically realizable, concentrated vorticity structure in Navier-Stokes flow that can travel macroscopic distances.

title: Critical GJMS Equations on $\mathbb{H}^n \times \mathbb{S}^m$
summary:
Let $M=\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{S}^m$, where $n\geq 2$, $m\geq 1$, and $N=n+m$. Let $P_k$ be the order-$2k$ GJMS operator, with $1\leq k<N/2$, and assume that $Λ_0=\infσ_{L^2(M)}(P_k)>0$. We study$$P_kU-λU=|U|^{q-2}U,\qquad q=\frac{2N}{N-2k},\qquad 0<λ\leqΛ_0,$$and attainment of the associated critical quotient $S_{λ,k}(M)$.
  Let $S_{N,k}$ be the Euclidean best Sobolev constant. For $0<λ<Λ_0$, the inequality $S_{λ,k}(M)<S_{N,k}$ implies attainment and a nontrivial weak solution. Localized Euclidean extremals establish this inequality when $N\geq4k$, or when $2k+2\leq N<4k$ and $λ>Λ_{\mathrm{loc}}$, where $Λ_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is explicit. If $N\geq2k+2$ and $S_{Λ_0,k}(M)<S_{N,k}$, attainment also holds at $λ=Λ_0$ in the threshold form completion.
  At the threshold, $L^2$-coercivity fails precisely on the constant spherical eigenspace. We combine cocompactness for its hyperbolic coefficient with a profile decomposition relative to the critical transformations preserving $\mathcal{A}=\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times{0}$. Under the threshold hypotheses above, the strict Euclidean inequality excludes concentration escaping $\mathcal{A}$ from normalized minimizing sequences. If $r_j^{(J)}$ denotes the remainder after the first $J$ extracted profiles, then$$\lim_{J\to\infty}\limsup_{j\to\infty}|r_j^{(J)}|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^N)}=0,$$which yields compactness modulo the axis-preserving transformations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies critical elliptic equations involving GJMS operators on product manifolds $\mathbb{H}^n \times \mathbb{S}^m$, establishes conditions for the attainment of optimal Sobolev constants, and proves compactness of minimizing sequences via profile decomposition with axis-preserving transformations.
AI.motivation: To understand when the critical Sobolev quotient $S_{\lambda,k}(M)$ is attained on non-compact product manifolds, particularly when $L^2$-coercivity fails at the threshold $\lambda = \Lambda_0$.
AI.method: Profile decomposition relative to axis-preserving transformations preserving $\mathcal{A}=\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times\{0\}$, cocompactness for hyperbolic coefficient, and Euclidean extremal localization.
AI.result: For $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$, $S_{\lambda,k}(M)<S_{N,k}$ implies attainment; holds when $N\geq 4k$ or $2k+2\leq N<4k$ with $\lambda>\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$. At $\lambda=\Lambda_0$, attainment holds if $S_{\Lambda_0,k}(M)<S_{N,k}$, with remainder $L^q$-norm vanishing as $J\to\infty$.
AI.conclusion: Compactness of minimizing sequences is achieved modulo axis-preserving transformations, overcoming the failure of $L^2$-coercivity at the threshold.

title: Eigenfunctions, free boundaries, and time-frequency localization
summary:
We develop an inverse theory for time-frequency localization operators, whose central idea that of is free-boundary problem: the localization domain is unknown and its boundary is recovered from prescribed spectral data. The approach is based on the principle that an eigenfunction may be regarded as geometric data which determines a localization domain, and prescribing it has strong consequences for the associated variational problem.
  Four main results follow from this main framework. First, if $f_0$ is a polynomial sufficiently close to the Gaussian and $λ\in(0,1)$, we construct a real-analytic domain $U_λ$ such that $f_0$ is an eigenfunction of the localization operator associated with $U_λ$ and with eigenvalue $λ$, giving a general inverse construction of localization domains, which is the first in the literature. Second, we recover the null-set invariant Abreu-Dörfler characterization of disks as the only localization domains of Hermite polynomials in the simply connected case. Third, we prove optimality of the exponent $1/2$ in the Gómez-Guerra-Ramos-Tilli quantitative stability inequality, answering thus a question posed by those authors. Finally, we show that local maximizers of the Gaussian Faber-Krahn problem are disks, which extends the Nicola-Tilli concentration inequality to the local case as well, and, as a matter of fact, as a consequence of a Fock space concentration-compactness profile decomposition, we are able to use this to give a new, different proof of the Nicola-Tilli theorem.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an inverse theory for time-frequency localization operators using free-boundary problems, constructing localization domains from eigenfunctions and deriving four major results including inverse domain construction, characterization of disks, optimal stability exponents, and local Faber-Krahn maximizers.
AI.motivation: To establish an inverse theory for time-frequency localization operators where the localization domain is unknown and recovered from spectral data, filling a gap in the literature where no such inverse construction previously existed.
AI.method: The approach treats eigenfunctions as geometric data that determine localization domains via a free-boundary problem framework, using variational principles and Fock space concentration-compactness profile decomposition.
AI.result: (1) Construction of real-analytic domains from polynomial eigenfunctions close to Gaussian; (2) Recovery of the Abreu-Dörfler disk characterization for Hermite polynomials; (3) Proof of optimality of exponent 1/2 in Gómez-Guerra-Ramos-Tilli stability inequality; (4) Local maximizers of Gaussian Faber-Krahn problem are disks, with a new proof of the Nicola-Tilli theorem.
AI.conclusion: The inverse theory provides a unified framework yielding fundamental results in localization operators, stability inequalities, and concentration inequalities, with implications for time-frequency analysis and spectral geometry.

title: An Eyring--Kramers Law for the Hypoelliptic Third-Order Langevin Diffusion
summary: We prove an Eyring--Kramers law for metastable transitions of the hypoelliptic third-order Langevin diffusion in the low-temperature limit. The model is motivated by the high-order Langevin diffusion of Mou et al. (2021, J. Mach. Learn. Res., 22(42), 1--41). The model has a Gibbs invariant measure, but the noise reaches the position variable only through a step-three chain. For a double-well potential with a unique index-one transition saddle, we determine both the Arrhenius exponential scale and the sharp prefactor of the mean transition time. The prefactor is governed by the unique positive unstable rate of the third-order deterministic linearization at the saddle. Our proof extends the underdamped Eyring--Kramers strategy of Lee--Ramil--Seo (2026, arXiv:2503.12610v2) to the step-three setting and combines the weak-capacity framework with a saddle-adapted boundary layer, an explicit Gaussian current calculation, committor localization, and intrawell flatness. Under matched kinetic normalizations, the resulting metastable prefactor is strictly smaller than its underdamped counterpart. A numerical experiment for a one-dimensional double well illustrates both the Arrhenius scaling and the predicted prefactor comparison.

AI.tldr: This paper proves an Eyring-Kramers law for metastable transitions in a hypoelliptic third-order Langevin diffusion at low temperatures, determining both the Arrhenius exponential scale and the sharp prefactor, which is smaller than the underdamped counterpart.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by the high-order Langevin diffusion model of Mou et al. (2021), aiming to understand metastable transition behavior in hypoelliptic systems where noise reaches the position variable only through a step-three chain.
AI.method: The proof extends the underdamped Eyring-Kramers strategy of Lee-Ramil-Seo (2026) to the step-three setting, combining weak-capacity framework with saddle-adapted boundary layer, explicit Gaussian current calculation, committor localization, and intrawell flatness.
AI.result: For a double-well potential with a unique index-one transition saddle, both the Arrhenius exponential scale and the sharp prefactor (governed by the unique positive unstable rate of the third-order deterministic linearization at the saddle) are determined. The prefactor is strictly smaller than its underdamped counterpart under matched kinetic normalizations.
AI.conclusion: The Eyring-Kramers law is established for the hypoelliptic third-order Langevin diffusion, with numerical experiments confirming the Arrhenius scaling and predicted prefactor comparison.

title: Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov inclusions of the mean field type
summary: The paper studies a dynamical system in the Wasserstein space, where the evolution is governed by a Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation with coefficients chosen from a prescribed set that depends at each point on that point and on the current measure. Under the assumption that the multivalued mapping determining the constraints is convex-valued, upper semicontinuous and satisfies certain growth conditions, we prove an existence theorem and establish the compactness of the solution set. Moreover, we study an optimal control problem for such dynamical systems.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a dynamical system in Wasserstein space governed by a Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation with state- and measure-dependent coefficients. Under convex-valued, upper semicontinuous, and growth constraints, it proves existence and compactness of solutions, and studies an optimal control problem.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous existence and compactness theory for dynamical systems in Wasserstein space where the drift/diffusion coefficients depend on both spatial location and the current probability measure, under general multivalued constraints.
AI.method: The authors model the system as a differential inclusion in Wasserstein space governed by a Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation, assuming the coefficient mapping is convex-valued, upper semicontinuous, and satisfies growth conditions. Existence and compactness are proved via analytical techniques, and an optimal control framework is formulated.
AI.result: An existence theorem for solutions of the constrained dynamical system is proved, along with compactness of the solution set. The optimal control problem for such systems is also studied.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a theoretical foundation for measure-dependent dynamical systems with multivalued constraints, extending existing results to more general settings and opening avenues for optimal control of such systems.

title: Two-phase source and reaction coefficient Stefan type problems
summary: This paper investigates inverse two-phase Stefan-type problems for parabolic heat equations with unknown time-dependent source and reaction coefficients. Suitable transformations reduce the original free-boundary problems to equivalent equations on fixed spatial domains, and Fourier spectral expansions are used to derive reconstruction formulas for the unknown coefficients. In the first formulation, the source coefficients are identified from integral, pointwise, and nonlocal additional data, leading to Volterra integral equations. In the second formulation, an exponential transformation is applied to recover the reaction coefficients. A principal advantage of the model with two moving boundaries is that each boundary provides its own Stefan condition which sufficient to determine the two unknown time-dependent coefficients without additional overdetermination conditions. Under appropriate assumptions the existence, uniqueness, boundedness and regularity of weak and strong solutions are established. Illustrative examples confirm the applicability of the reconstruction procedure and show that the coefficients remain stable under the noisy data. The proposed approach provides a rigorous base for identifying time-dependent thermal parameters in two-phase phase-change processes.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method for solving inverse Stefan-type problems with unknown time-dependent source/reaction coefficients using Fourier spectral expansions and transformations to fixed domains, proving existence, uniqueness, and stability of solutions.
AI.motivation: To develop a rigorous mathematical framework for identifying unknown time-dependent thermal parameters (source and reaction coefficients) in two-phase phase-change (Stefan) problems without requiring additional overdetermination conditions.
AI.method: The authors apply suitable transformations to convert free-boundary problems to fixed spatial domains, use Fourier spectral expansions to derive reconstruction formulas for unknown coefficients, and employ Volterra integral equations (for source coefficients) or exponential transformations (for reaction coefficients). Two moving boundaries each provide a Stefan condition, eliminating the need for extra overdetermination.
AI.result: Existence, uniqueness, boundedness, and regularity of weak and strong solutions are established under appropriate assumptions. Illustrative examples confirm applicability and show that coefficients remain stable under noisy data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach provides a rigorous foundation for identifying time-dependent thermal parameters in two-phase phase-change processes, with demonstrated stability against noise.
